channel.title: Adam Curry's Daily Source Code Podcast
channel.description: The Daily Source Code, Adam Curry's podcast that started podcasting. From August 2004 to November 2013: 863 episodes plus specials, recorded from Belgium, Guildford, San Francisco and on the road. News, technology, music and life, and a new medium being built in real time, with listener promos, voicemails and podsafe music. The complete archive, restored, with transcripts and chapters for every episode.

item.dc:creator: Adam Curry
item.description:
Daily Source Code for Thursday April 26th 2012 Remembering The Ones We Lost
Remembering The Ones We Lost Remembering the one's we lost I got so drunk tonite and after watching half of American Idol raping Queen songs, I decided it was time to bring back a good old DSC to cheer up the vibe. Thanks to Ms Micky for the support, encouragement and drinks. Thanks to Bobbi Eden for the bonerage Thansk to the Human Resources in the chat room for keeping me company Thank you Silicon Spin for the artwork
Thanks to Jack Daniels Than you Max Factor for my makeup Thanks to all the artists we love and miss Duration: 02:27:25

item.title: Daily Source Code for Friday March 14th 2008
item.itunes:title: Daily Source Code for Friday March 14th 2008
item.dc:creator: Adam Curry
item.description:
#733 Daily Source Code for Friday March 14th 2008

If I am only able to bring you one show in a particularly busy week, it darn well better be a Fubar Friday an I think I delivered today. 2 main topics to discuss: Why the hell haven't I been doing shows this week, what's going on? The answer comes in two parts... One is my road trip and some interesting mainstream media action, the other and most important is the focused strategy and direction PodShow has embarked on. I go into deep detail on our business model, where the money comes from and how you can get your hands on that stream of revenue as an independent producer of audio and video properties. Please don't get me wrong though, the show is like a freight train runnin' at breakneck speed, mainly thanks to the music, Sir Jersey Todd and the HitTest, all carefully selected for your listening pleasure.

Music in this episode:

Bruce Springsteen - Hungry Heart

item.description:
#726 Daily Source Code for Wednesday February 20th 2008

The 'Batteries Not Included' episode of the DSC is once again one for the history books. I feel that the 'live' aspect is working well. Almost real-time reports of the missleblowingthe sattelite out of space as well as the meteor strike in Washington state. Some great calls about the state of the nations Uk and USA (patriotic stuff here) and an invite to get thrown in jail for a night on 'the rock'. item.title: Daily Source Code for Friday February 08th 2008
item.itunes:title: Daily Source Code for Friday February 08th 2008
item.dc:creator: Adam Curry
item.description:
#720 Daily Source Code for Friday February 8th 2008

Fubar Friday's on the Daily Source Code are typically compiled of great music to get the weekend started with. Although today is no exception, we run a bit long due to two major rants: The British Surveillance Society (The Snoop Dogg Nation) and three reports on the Homeland Security Administration. The first is the TSAweblog, who admitted this week that they were at fault in San Francisco forrequiringall electronic gadgets to be removed from hand luggage. The second is the EFF'slawsuitagainst the Customs and Border Protection agency, who did not respond on time to a Freedom of information request. ThePDFof the suit is a fantastic read and you can see my story all over it. Finally, and perhaps the most frightening is the apparent arming of the TSA with small side weapons as is made clear by theirrecent purchaseof small arms simulators.

Music in the show today from:

JTX - PArty Like A Rockstar
Stranglers - No More Heroes

It’s Sunday afternoon at the cottage and whilst clearing out my closets and drawers, I cracked open my old PowerBook G$, which contained a semi-finished interview with 3 partners of venture capital firm Kleiner Perkins: John Doerr, Ray Lane and Bill Joy. The reason for the interview was the firm’s annoncement of a $100 million fund for ‘Green’ technologies.

If you want to learn more about venture capital funding and the people behind it, then this is a must listen. If you’re calling about Giselle, this probably isn’t for you

Just returned from San Francisco, got in around 10am and agreed with Patricia that we would hold off on ‘updating’ each other until I had reinstalled the studio for a show.

#433 Daily Source Code for Wednesday August 2nd 2006

My last sunrise this trip from the Curry Condo in San Francisco, Ca.

A quick wrap up of the past 3 weeks of my visit, as I prepare to fly home to my girls this afternoon.
Just in time for th trip, Amy Mac, from the Fitness Attack helps me with a personalized
workout program ‘Adam’s Assercize’, be prepared to follow along with her expert instructions!
There’s trouble in Hollywood with the unions thats brewing and I try to explain this amazing
multi-touch computing demo I saw on the TED feed, you gotta check it out for yourself.

item.title: Podshow Xmas Part 1
item.itunes:title: Podshow Xmas Part 1
item.dc:creator: Adam Curry
item.description:
First in a series of mixed podsafe music holiday songs. Just subscribe to the feed and you’ll have a nice collection for the holidays!

In order to respect the rights of the owners of the songs, I will be mixing two songs together with a holiday greeting from podcasters and podsafe artists in each episode. This should still give some good serendipity when you put your mp3 player on shuffle mode. Encoding is at 128kps for better quality.

To kick it off we hear from Podsafe for Peace and Jill Parr.

Part 1

[Site ] - GeekIn_Promo_1 Cirrus vs Cessna - Cirrus may be a sexy, modern plane, but the biggest problem I am hearing from other pilots that are looking to buy one is the Cirrus' longevity. The Cirrus is a composite airplane. It's value drops over time whereas the Cessna's does not. I used to fly a 1957 Cessna 182 and almost none of the major components had been replaced. That won't be true with a composite plane. I have flown the Katana and the Cirrus and they are great planes, they just won't stand the test of time as well. A Cirrus is fun to fly for it's modernness and sexyness, it's just not an investment. I bagged my last girlfriend with a Cirrus. Picked her up from work in it for a sunset flight. item.itunes:summary: Daily Source Code for Friday September 9th 2005 #238 - From Curry Cottage, Guildford, United Kingdom - Shownotes Full Outline Mashup: Bass211 - Oblateeth via [MashupTown ] CastBlaster Mike chat PodShow Alley? No Damn Announcement on DSC? - Hey AC, So rather than stir up controvery and talking behind ya back talk Podcast Alley and other forums about the acquisition. I'll just ask directly... A lot folks (not me) were surprised about the acquisition. Maybe you can say a few words on the DSC now that the deal is done. Cheers, Jeff -- Podcast Shuffle Show Web: www.podcastshuffle.com RSS: feeds.feedburner.com—PodcastShuffleShow Skepticality co-host in hospital - Derek is in hospital. Swoopy explains - the_message Posafe: Rob Costlo - I Do [Info ] Promo: I miss blighty [Site ] Promo: BFBS Multimedia [Site ] CV-Casts DSC Sept. 7 - Ham Operators - Adam, Just a note to say thanks for acknowledging the work that the ham operators have been doing since the storm hit New Orleans last week. There have been a number of stories in the media about how they are helping to keep communication lines open during this devastating period of time. While there are a number of HF communication nets running constantly, there are also a couple of services that use Voice over IP as their primary method of communication. Have a look at the Internet Radio Linking Project (www.irlp.net ) and the Voice over IP Weather Net (www.voipwx.net ) as examples. Both of these sites offer streaming audio of the communications when the nets are active, as they probably will be next week when the next storms start making their way west. And just as an aside, Morse code is no longer required for access to some parts of the ham spectrum in the US, and is not required at all up here in Canada. Thanks for a great show, Adam. I listen to it every day on the commute to work. 73, Rod Templeton, VE7RJT Vancouver, BC RevTim Katrina hope message - rtp-KatrinaHopeMessage Feedback on Hotel Podcast - Hi Adam, just listened to your hotel podcast..had'nt heard u before..u got potential....but do ya self a favour..get ya self a producer!.....bit too much dribble, dribble, dribble....having said that....let me say this..keep going. regards Warren ATKINSON Perth, AUSTRALIA You made my roadtrip! - Adam, For the last week I vacationed in the Colorado Rocky Moutnains. We opted to drive there (rather than fly) and the trek was around 1100 miles from Austin, TX to Estes Park, CO no matter how you cut it. I loaded up a couple weeks worth of The Daily Source Code into my iPod (with FM iTrip) and you kept me company on my journey, driving into the night. I must say that I've never been so entertained for such a long period of time! It's amazing how intimate of an experience it is hearing your voice rambling "to me" while driving on a dark highway at 70 mph around 3am while my kids and wife sleep in the seats next to me. I couldn't have done the trip without you and your daily source. So thank you for such a great podcast, always. I've attached a song that I think you'll find more than perfect for The Daily Source Code. It's an independant band's song so you should have no copyright infringement issues wiht playing it on your show. Enjoy DICK N JANE : Not the way you Need Their website is : www.dicknjanetheband.com—home.html Rock on, Adam, Merrell - DICK_N_JANE-Not_The_Way_You PodSafe: Dick and Jane - Not the way you need [Site ] - San Francisco's GRIDDLE just released its second album, Turning Violet, with a southwestern tour that took the boys across Texas. Members Kimo Ball, Xifer Fortier, Chris McGrew, and Kevin Seal enjoy volume, alcohol, melodies and confusion. Their songs are strange but catchy. More at Griddle. Podsafe Music Network

item.itunes:summary: Daily Source Code for Thursday September 8th 2005 #237 - From Curry Cottage, Guildford, United Kingdom - Shownotes Full Outline Mashup: Team9 - Gets you going after a long weekend! via [MashupTown ] - Team9 gets you going after a long weekend. Simple A+B Mashup of Belinda Carlisle and Graham Coxon. - To Get you Goin' after a long weekend The honeymoon is over with Virgin Atlantic CastBlaster [Site ] Checkout @ The St Regis Club Promo: Podshock [Site ] - Podshock Promo Promo: FratPack Podcast - FPT-Promo-1min-Aug2005 Sirius sept. 29th, Operation PodSquad Birthday Song from some Queercasters - FROM: Twinkelboi John Ong- Ongline Podcast Cheryl Mercowski and Wanda Wisdom from LBR Patrick and Noah Show Marshal Click- Gayborhood Radio Podcastique and Madge and everyone at qpodder.org! - curryday Arbitron Ratings - Hey, Adam! Talk about interesting, I just got a letter in the mail from Arbitron (the US ratings folks). They want me to participate in their “radio station” survey! I’m gonna say yes, but I’m gonna log my PODCAST listening right along side the ‘traditional’ radio! And I already know I listen to either podcasts or streaming internet radio much more often than over-the-air stations. I’ll keep you posted! I bet they don’t even have a podcast section yet. I’ll make sure we get that changed! My rating period starts on 9/22/2005. Cheers! -=\ Bob Robinson \=- Subliminal Experiment Worked -- sort of - Hi Adam, Normally I listed to the DSC in the car on my way to work, so you had the right idea with your subliminal experiment. Unfortunately, I listed to that particular show in bed before going to sleep. So, when you asked us to focus on an object, all I saw was darkness. The experiment was not a complete failure. That night I head a dream I was walking through an airport. I sat down to wait for my flight and decided to strike up a conversation with the traveler next to me. His name? Adam Curry... Kevin Crossman Fremont, CA The Frat Pack Tribute Podcast at www.fratpackpodcast.com Great jobcast...what about CVCast - Adam, I really enjoyed the jobcast, but was really surprised when the guys asked candidates to send in a "paper" CV. How about CVcasts, where the candidate adds the CV as show notes, but then uses 10-15mins to tell the company about themselves...would be a great way to really shorten the recruitment cycle. The thing I got from the jobcast was that these guys sounded like people I would like to work for, so I guess it might work in reverse, so that they hear someone they want to work for them....just an idea.... rgds Mark Help IS Here NOW...I've Seen It - Hi Adam, I was listening to your show as you were talking about the "instant relief" we expect in America. You played a promo by Chris Rockwell and in it he said " these people are not getting the help they need to survive". I'm sorry, but that's not the case. What Chris is seeing on TV is only a small amount of the people who are just now getting help. Why? Because some have been hiding in their homes not wanting to leave. They simply thought the water would go down quickly or because they wanted to protect what little they have left. One person told me he had plenty of food and water but was afraid to leave because of the "bad element" that was shooting at the rescuers and evacuees. I know this because I've spoken with many of the evacuees at the Red Cross shelter here in Shreveport. Yesterday I spent 4 hours just talking to Red Cross volunteers and refugees that just got out of New Orleans in the past 24 hours. You played one of my interviews on your show last Friday. ( ZIP 71101 with Ron Stroope) I spoke to a girl named Tammy. She had no idea if her father and mother was safe because they stayed behind. Yesterday, as I was leaving I spotted her. She told me that the Red Cross found her father and he was working with FEMA and they got him a place to live for his family in Lafayette, LA. He will pick up her and her twin brother today. I searched for the other people I spoke to on my first visit and they were not there. I was told that they probably found a place to live or maybe a family took them in. Many have gone back to south Louisiana to stay with family and friends. Yesterday many of the local companies held a job fair and many found employment. In fact, I saw one lady jumping for joy as she was telling her fellow refugees that she had a job. This shelter is housing over 1200 people. I know of another one housing about the same. On the LSU campus in Shreveport another shelter has been opened. Many of the local volunteers are taking people home with them or finding them places to live. I visited a church that bought out a mall. In the old Dillard's area there were hundreds of boxes stacked 6 feet high full of clothing, furniture and supplies like bottled water. This area must have been over 75,000 square feet or more and it was nearly full. Another church took another building about the same size and they are filling it up and giving it out. I'll tell these stories and more on my next podcast. I can tell you first hand, it's happening through the efforts and generosity of the people. We should never wait or depend on the government to take the first step in something like this. There will always be some folks that get missed or overlooked and that's a shame. Of course, I'm only seeing what's happening in my city but I'm 100 percent sure that in Austin, Dallas, Houston, Baton Rouge, Jackson, Atlanta, or anywhere there are shelters and concerned citizens getting involved, help will be available. It's a slow process and will be even slower and harder for many of the elderly and handicapped but I believe this country will pull together and find a solution, because together, we can make a difference. Ron Stroope Podsafe: Rob Costlow - Bliss [Info ] - Hello! I let another song into the Podsafe Music Network. A long…………….. one. I wrote it for my wife, for our wedding. It’s called “Bliss” and it’s in my info. Played it for her during the ceremony… 6 years ago, this Oct. 2 (yah, we got married young). Something that may inspire, give meaning to the unknown. I really wish I could do more for the utter crap that’s going on in the US. Crap that’s unavoidable devastation and other regular political poo. Don’t get me started. Thank God there is a lot of support from citizens. More to come. I hope you enjoy. Rob - Rob_Costlow_-_Bliss Podsafe Music Network Podcaster Terms HitTest #57 [Site ] - hittest57

item.itunes:summary: Daily Source Code for Friday September 2nd 2005 #234 - From Curry Cottage, Guildford, United Kingdom - Shownotes Full Outline Thank God it's Friday! - Thanks Victor Alberts! - Thank_God_It's_Friday Mashup: Dreaming in your sleep via [MashupTown ] - Dreaming_in_Your_Sleep_brought_ iTunes affiliate! - Thanks to Andrew Machado! Thanks to Tom Hickey at WinningSupplies.com The new Outline Process Daily Download [Site ] - Daily Download 08_31_2005 - She doesn't care about the show Katrina - PW's special edition of Digital Flotsam [Show Link ] - Reaction on Katarina - Hi Adam, I would like to reflect on your call for help for the people in New Orleans. First of all I want to say that it must be horrible to encounter and I certainly don't want it to happen to me. But (and yes there is allways a but) yesterday also 900+ iraq people died on a bridge. And I am not hearing anybody care about that, what makes Americans more important than the people of Iraque? Most of those Americans have money and are insured but those poor citizens of iraque have nothing. The goal of my message is not to upset the people in New Orleans but to try to open the eyes of all the other people in the world. To let them see how much they are being manipulated by the media, the media acts like the many people in Iraq dying are just numbers but when it are Americans or citizens of any other western nation are special and the coverage is more emotional and personal in order to get many people involved. I plee for a more objective coverage of the news because todays journalism is not real journalism anymore it is more sensation and subjective coverage than nice objective coverage which is assisted by evidence. So far my opinion on todays journalism i would like to here your reflections on this. Greetings Basiel - Hurricane PSA from Frank Truth - Hurricane Relief Message - Katrina PSA - HurricaneProject.org - KATRINAPSA2 - Gillmor Gang PSA - GGKatrinaPSA - Richard Bluestein feedback - yrhurricainereport - Zip7101 Podcast: Conversations with survivors of Hurricane Katrina [Site ] - zip16 - RnR Geek PSA - Hurricanerelief - How the Podcast community could create NOLA relief fund by itself - Hi Adam I had a thought about how the Podcast Community (PC) - or at least part of it - could create real money for the NOLA relief effort. My idea is that several key players in the PC could each contribute 5 minutes to a Podcast and the resulting mega-cast could be sold for (say) ten bucks via iTunes with the proceeds going to NOLA. For example you could kick off the show, and then had over the resulting file to PJ Fenton who would hand over to Dawn and Drew who would hand it off to Madge who would hand over to Wichitaw Rutherford etc etc - and the resulting show would be a "collectors item" only available for a limited period. This wouldn't take long to put together as the file could just be played in CastBlaster by each participant before they add their bit and then pass on the file+1! The iTunes DRM would stop mass file sharing and because it wouldn't be around for a long it would encourage folks to download it NOW. I am in UK so feel kind of impotent to do anything material to help from here but I thought this would be a neat way of getting the PC to deliver for NOLA from its mass listenership. What do you think? Best regards Paul Parkinson theflashing12 podcast at www.theflashing12.com - Podshow Hurricane Relief Message [Link ] Promo: Chub Creek [Site ] - ChubCreekKickItPromo HitTest#56 [Site ] - hittest56 Promo: Reaching for lucidity [Site ] - ReachingforLucidityPromo questions regarding new podcasters - Hi Adam, I'm sure this one of many many emails you've recieved from newbies such as myself. First off, The past few months have literally changed my whole perspective on things. When iTunes 4.9 came out, I was introduced (finally) to the wonderful world of podcasting. I'll be honest Adam. I feel I can and will make a name for myself in podcasting. There is one problem though, when it comes to the tech side of things, I don't know where to start. Is simplly want to put out a quality sounding show where I can talk to the listeners, play them kick ass music that they should be hearing but aren't, and maybe make somebody laugh they're ass off from time to time. That's not too much to ask, is it? Not that you wouldn't, but I feel I like I may not get a reply from you due to the volume of emails you must recieve. However, if anyone would have the right answer to my question, it would be Adam Curry. I'm a PC user (boo hiss). I know I know. I'll have a mac soon if it fucking kills me. Anyway, I was wondering what the best software for a PC user/ beginning podcaster could use to produce a quality show. I can't say money is no object, but I'm not exactly starving. Also, can you recommend a website or book where I can get information on how to set up a feed, get a server, etc . I realize you are a busy man Adam, but any info you may be able to provide would be much appreciated. I know this is a bit long but I have to tell you this. I must congratulate you for the wonderful things you've managed to accomplish. I'm 33 I remember you on Headbangers Ball. I never would have guessed that that guy from MTV would help create the next movement. I truly want, no, need to be a part of this. I feel podcasting is going to literally change the way we percieve the media. I just love the idea that average people, Dawn & Drew for instance, can touch people and be successful simply for being themselves. I obviously could go on and on. If you've gotten this far, thank you so much for your time. I love the DSC and enjoy your show on Sirius. Keep up the fantastic work that you do. I hope this doesn't make me come off as a kiss-ass. I'm just bouncing off the walls, driving my wife and kids mad trying to figure out how to get into this. Cheers! See you at the Expo in Ontario. Respect, Dan Ramirez Soundvertising - That Senseo moment - Adam, I listen to the DSC at work(!) so when you did the Senseo thing I was looking at my screen (AS/400 RPG ILE code, if you want to know). That means I now get even more distracted than ever! Thanks ;-). But it's worth it. Renato. - Remembering Podcasts at Certain Landmarks - Hey Adam! I am a teenager but I am not going to talk about the teenager conversation. I try to make a little money over the summer by cutting lawns. To help past the time while cutting the lawns, I listen to podcasts. Normally I follow the same pattern when cutting a certain lawn. I have experienced the same thing as DGA (is that right?) when I get to a certain point when cutting a lawn. I remember something someone said or an interesting conversation in a podcast when I reach that point the next time I cut that lawn. I feel a little better now that I know other people have the same problem. Best of luck with Podshow, Sean Birthday - Promo: Bari Koral Site ] - happy-birthday-adam-from-bari-koral - My 2 year old son wishing you an early Happy Birthday! - Devon Ostendorf Hey Adam, My son Kaden has such a tremendous interest in talking into the microphone that he is considering starting his own podcast. Though he isn't allowed to listen to your show quite yet, I told him you had inspired many to get started on their own shows and that you had a birthday coming up. He thought you might appreciate an early Happy Birthday greeting so here it is! Hope you have a good one, Devon P.S. I don't have a server handy at the moment to plop this file out on, so hopefully this doesn't foul up your inbox too much - it is not terribly large. Sorry.. - HappyBdayAdamCurry - Happy Birthday Christina - Judefan Hope this doesn't fill up your g-mail Still working on getting him to say PodFather so your birthday wish may be a little late. Keep it real -- lovehouseradio.com subscribe at: lovehouseradio.libsyn.com—rss - HappyBirthdayChristina - Biddies Hurricane relief & B'day greeting - Happy Birthday Adam

item.itunes:summary: Daily Source Code for Thursday September 1st 2005 #233 - From Curry Cottage, Guildford, United Kingdom - Shownotes Full Outline Mashup: The Dog Smells like Roses - 99x via [MashupTown ] Apple iTunes Your iTunes Affiliate Application Status - Dear Adam Curry: We regret to inform you that iTunes has chosen not to accept your application for the iTunes Affiliate Program at this time. This may be because: -- The content is unrelated to iTunes -- Your site is temporarily down or under construction ¿-please make sure to apply again after 2 weeks. -- A wrong or misspelled URL given in the application. Please correct the problem and apply again. -- Your site is aesthetically unpleasing -- Your site promotes tobacco, alcoholic beverages or excessive drinking/drug use -- Your site contains extreme religious content -- Your site is international (with a majority of visitors based OUTSIDE the US. or written in a foreign language) If any of the above problematic criteria can be resolved, we look forward to your reapplication. If you plan to reapply in the next two weeks, you must do so at the following link because of restrictions by the LinkShare network. Please reapply and we will gladly reconsider. alogin.linksynergy.com—sterm.shtml If you have any questions or concerns, please feel free to email us at itunesaffiliates@apple.com or contact@linkshare.com. Thank you for your interest in the iTunes Affiliate Program. Best Regards, iTunes Affiliate Team www.itunes.com—affiliates Bar Stool Today! - Tom Hickey Is mijn podcast ervaring uniek? - Dag Adam, Ik download al sinds januari je podcast en vind je gebabbel leuk om naar te luisteren, vooral als er Nederlands gesproken wordt. Ik vraag mij af of er nog mensen zijn die hetzelfde ervaren als ze naar podcasts luisteren, spreek er eens over tijdens je podcast: I listen a lot to podcasts when I walk to the office and when I work out: running, riding my mountainbike and race-bike, bouldering, ... I've noticed that locations can trigger my memory about a particular podcast. It happened again today: I rode my mountainbike along a route I take frequently (west of Brussels) and at a certain road crossing I remembered a discussion about a new tablet PC on the Tablet PC Show I had listened to the previous time I rode past that location. It's a kind of reverse soundseeing: things I see trigger sounds I heard. Have you experienced this or have people mentioned this to you? Thanks for the show, en wanneer komt er nog een PPP? Didier Stevens, Brussel PSA: Katrina wichita Promo: Gaming Edge Weekly DS and GBA explained - Michael Shotter Hello, I'm sure plenty of other nerds will jump on this, but I figured I'd join the chorus. The DS is the "Nintendo DS," Nintendo's latest handheld gaming device. The letters DS refer to the system's Dual Screens, which allow unique display and input options for games. The GBA is the GameBoy Advance, which was Nintendo's previous handheld system, still in wide use by gamers and backward compatible with original GameBoy games. For more information on current gaming platforms and operating systems, check out our State of the Game article on Gaming's Edge. www.gamingsedge.com—viewcontent.cfm ? content=21&content_type=Article&department=1 And yes, I'm going to bug you again about playing the promo for our "Gaming's Edge Weekly Roundup" podcast. Here's a direct link to the promo: www.gamingsedge.com—gewrpromo.mp3 and our podcasting info page: www.gamingsedge.com—info.html Hope this is useful. Michael Shotter (a.k.a. VorTech) Katrina relief auctions going on right now - Dear Mr. Curry, (I know you're not THAT old) :) I was listening to your podcast this morning when you spoke of Hurricane Katrina and asking for us to let you know of any ways that people can help the victims of this devastation. My new podcast Boutique Café is almost ready to launch and we'll be doing a show late this week about hurricane Katrina and how people can help and get involved. Our Boutique Selling community is vast and a big hearted group. Many of our fellow designers that we know have lost their homes and all their possessions. Fellow designers have joined together to give from our hearts. Please go to eBay and search "Boutique Angels", these talented designers are donating 100% of the proceeds through the verifiable eBay charity association of Mission Fish to MERCY CORPS - Hurricane Katrina fund. These sellers are giving of their talents, time, and materials to making some beautiful boutique items so please ask your listeners to check the auctions out and bid on some gorgeous one of a kind items to support Mercy Corps and those that need so much right now. Sincerely, Daria Muirhead Boutique Café www.boutiquecafe.com Biodiesel - Crap in your Tank - I love your biodiesel idea about being able to crap in your tank. I think we need to talk to Roto-rooter about some joint development of this technology. I mean, if they're pumping the stuff out of my septic tank already, why can't they pump it back into my gas tank. Of course, if the cooking oil biodiesel smells like french fries... _____________________________ Bill Lefler Podsafe Music Network Podcaster Terms MTV VMA's - James Martin actually I found out that Sean combs didn't give "his" watch to the guy in the audience well he did but after that during the commercial break a security guard came down and asked him to take the watch and they did give him a watch but it was a cheap knockoff of the actual watch. Biddies Live "Famous" [Site ] Kids complaining about parents - Hi, I'm a 17 year old teen from Australia and just wanted to pipe in that not all parents are horrible! Since I'm a fourth child (catholics...) my parents have pretty much accepted I'm going to grow up and that I want my privacy. That respect helps make a good relationship between my parents. Just thought I would tell you that not all parents and teens have hate each other! PodSafe: Griddle - Preoccupied [Site ] - San Francisco's GRIDDLE just released its second album, Turning Violet, with a southwestern tour that took the boys across Texas. Members Kimo Ball, Xifer Fortier, Chris McGrew, and Kevin Seal enjoy volume, alcohol, melodies and confusion. Their songs are strange but catchy. More at Griddle. HitTest #55 [Site ]

item.itunes:summary: Daily Source Code for Wednesday August 31st 2005 #232 - From Curry Cottage, Guildford, United Kingdom - Shownotes Full Outline Mashup: Macamuppet or the "The Doors Take A Walk Down Sesame Street" by Pilchard - The Doors, The Manamana Guy, and throw in a little Macarena. via MashupTown Using Email Addresses in Show Notes - Kevin Crossman I didn't like the new show notes format at first but do like seeing the text of the emails. So, I'm a net positive at this point. FYI: It wasn't a big deal for me, a podcaster who has his email address all over the net, but others might object to you posting their email addresses in the show notes (where they can be harvested by spam robots). You're spoiling us with all these daily Daily Source Codes. We appreciate it! Kevin Crossman The Frat Pack Tribute: Saluting Hollywood's Comedy Clique www.the-frat-pack.com Listen to our Podcast at www.fratpackpodcast.com Wichita PSA Dave's Lounge Katrina Relief PSA PSA Regarding Hurricane Katrina - mosspier Adam Curry: This is also from Radio NHCWX/Podweather.com/USA Weather Inc Anyone is free to play this on any media source, including Podcasts and The Daily Source Code. This is what effort we are doing at the station to help the victims of Hurricane Katrina. Thank you very much Michael W. Moss radio.nhcwx.com www.podweather.com usaweather.org www.podologist.com Donate to The Red Cross for Hurricane relief More on BioDiesel - Oil Supply - Mike Krus Hi this is Mike Krus, of newsisfree.com About the current state of oil supply, there's this thing called Tar Sands. It's basically oil which was not trapped under a non-porous layer of rocks, so the liquid & gas part has evaporated, leaving only tar in sand type soil. There is loads of that in Canada, more than in Gulf apparent. And we know exactly where it is. Getting the oil out of that is expensive though (you can't pump it, it's more like mining), would cost about $45 a barrel. But with the current price of oil, it would be economically viable. Of course, this means more oil related pollution for a longer time, with additional pollution produced while mining the damn thing... See en.wikipedia.org—Tar_sands www.wired.com—oil.html Anyway, great show... regards, Mike - pizza shop powers own car with bio-diesel - Tom Schuring Site - Not a Drop - Paul Clark Hey Adam, This may sound stupid, you can dismiss if you like, but I have been recieving numoerous emails about a rumor, about a "Not a Drop" day on September 1st, convincing people to not buy gas, forcing the oil companies to lower there prices. You live in the UK, you pay a lot more for "petrol" than we do here in the states. If you feel its a noteable cause, maybe give a little bleep out to your viewers. You have a strong voice in the community, make a difference. Even if not everyone does it, it will still make some ripples in the pond. Cirrus SR22 planes and test pilot - Nigel Savage Hey Adam, just listening to your show 231 and you mentioned the SR22 plane. My pal is a test pilot for it and I went up in it for a test flight with him. It's actually a great plane! don't knock it! You also mentioned the plane is destroyed after 'chute deployment and landing. This is not true, the landing gear only needed replacing in several tests performed in Minnesota, besides who gives a crap about the state of the plane when you survived what could have been a lethal crash. The chute does save lives and it's a great idea.. it WORKS! Keep up the great work and paint that Curry Complez brown or something, it's gotta look like wood at least Nigel I think guys (teens) are WAY different in mindset than girls - Rishabh Kumar Adam, Guy teens are MUCH MUCH MUCH MUCH MUCH different than girls....in mindset that is. Is it just me, or does it seem that more than 95% of advertisements on television directed to girls? Also, girls seem to do almost nothing but talk about fashion, and guys (hey, the guys part isn't THAT bad lol). Advertisements, in my opinion, are turning today's girls into fashion zombies. On the other hand, I'm not saying guys don't have their share of "weirdness" either. We dream about chicks more than half of the time, and need to get our lazy asses off of the ground at times. Both genders argue with their parents, and here's my view on it. For a guy teen, at least me, arguing with my parents seems to be an "every-other-day" sort of thing, and it feels commonplace nowadays. Our arguments seem to be more about our rights and why we're out with other people instead of "staying at home, with family" a lot. I agree with the other teens, parents DO seem to have a hard time "letting go". However, my arguments with my little brother (he is nine) seem to be much more frequent than with my parents. Anyways, I'm 14, and that's my 0.1 cents, Rishabh Kumar (pronounced Rish-ub) VMA's - Field Walsh Hey adam you never mentioned what you thought about this years VMA's on today show. I know that I thought they sucked ass, to damn much rap. I think they have gone way down hill ever since the year jimmy falon hosted them. I thought his montage opening skit was awsome, and I watch it every year expecting another awsome opening like that only to be disapointed. Oh yeah and how could you not like the cirrus sr-22? Its only the coolest GA plane out there, just look at that sweet panel! Even though I must say the 182RG is pretty cool also, i got about 30 hours in it. Later Field Walsh From Lee Wilkins - In da Club mp3 Licensing - Drew Sturgiss If you want to get around the mp3 licensing issue, a solution can be found in the ogg theora audio format. This is a lossy audio format, comparable to mp3, but completely without patents. It also boasts arguably better sound and compression. Anyhoo, just thought I'd let you know, thanks for doing the show, its like radio, but with perfect reception all the time. -- Drew Sturgiss DnD Full time! TV SCREEN BRAIN MELTING FACT :-)! - SeRgEy t Hi adam, its sergey again. first thing, happy birthday 2u. I wanted to tell you an interesting fact about TV screens, relating to what you said about the brain melting.... so: a friend of mine has been using computers for as long as he can remember, thats his job...and he used the first PC's, which had those green-black screens. The TV screens and the computer screens are basically the same thing, but, with the computers you just sit closer. anyways, he used his green black monitor every day, day after day for years. now his bald...and he started getting less hair in his early 20's.... noone in his familly had ever had problems like that.... after some reserch, in medical websites and books, he found out that that friken screen made the problem. what im basically trying to say is: TV screens DO IN SOME WAY MELTS YOUR BRAIN or atleast cause some health problems in the person.....and the closer you sit to it the more crap it does to ya. the last epesote was great, thanx alot for writing me back i was really happy to see that you did. later :-). Promo: TV Talk Podcast [Site ] Promo: Green Room Radio [Site ] Link of the Crime Scene Evidence Nintendo begins podcasting! - Walter Nintendo has just begun podcasting, K9Cast has the scoop: www.k9cast.com—more-on-nintendogsnintendos-first.html The timing of this is interesting because the Play-Yan mp3/multimedia add-on player for the Nintendo DS and GBA may see a US release date in "late 2005" according to wikipedia. Nintendo could be planning to turn DS and GBAs into podcast players! With over 50 million Gameboy Advance units sold that's alot of listeners! The first episode of the Nintendo Podcast is on the subject of Nintendogs, a virtual dog game (hence the interest to K9Cast). Excellent. Walter Listening to a podcast story - JP Dane-Castro Hey Adam. My name is JP and I have been a long time listener and fan of the Daily Source Code. First off I would just like to say happy birthday to you and your daughter Christina, congratulations to both of you. Second I would just like to say that a funny thing happened to me the other day. The car I was in drove under an overpass while I was listening to the latest installation of the Daily Source Code and for a split second I thought to myself "oh no, I am going to lose reception". I then immediately thought to myself "wait, this is a podcast, you can't lose reception." So there is the beauty of podcasting, being able to listen to what you want, when you want without having to worry about bad reception, or interceptions. So Adam I just thought that I would share that little tidbit of podcasting goodness with you, I love the show and keep up the good work! PodSafe: Zach Ashton - Tonite PMN Link - From The PodSafe Music Network [Site ] HitTest #54 [Site ]

item.itunes:summary: Daily Source Code for Tuesday August 30th 2005 #231 - From Curry Cottage, Guildford, United Kingdom Hurricane not as bad as expected? MTV Awards Mashup: Hollaback Girls Feel Good - Arty Fufkin [Site ] Driving music sales through podcasting - Two thoughts about driving music sales through mashups and hittests - Patrick Seemann pse@patom.ch to adam More options 6:35 am (9 hours ago) Hi Adam, I just want to add two thoughts to the topic: a) I listen to DSC on my commute which means that even when I like the music from mashups and hittests (and this happens often enough) I can't buy it right away. Back at home I usually don't know the title/artist anymore and don't have the time to relisten to DSC either. Would it be possible to list the songs used in the masups/hittests directly in the show notes? b) The best source to get mashup/hittest impact on music sales would be Apple/ITMS. Can't you use your contacts inside Apple to find out whether the sales number for a given title raises after it has been played in DSC? Kind regards, Patrick - Winwood on the HitTest - all your fault! - Jason Hollowed ben_nushmut@mac.com to adam More options 3:37 am (12 hours ago) Hey Adam, Just wanted to continue with the back-catalog line you brought up in DSC#230. I actually have the Winwood album Back in the High Life from iTunes already, but I was inspired to listen to it again after nearly a year away from it. OH MY GOD, I'm still amazed at how incredible Steve's voice was here. And as brilliant as Higher Love is, my personal connection goes straight to the title track. When I was born (October 28, 1986), that was the song playing on the radio when my dad got to see me for the first time. Even though I was I newborn at that moment, the song still resonates with me and actually brought me to tears in my dorm room as I listened to it (I was alone, but it wouldn't have mattered if I heard it with one or a dozen people in my room. It just reaches deep into my soul and brings out a part of me I'm still amazed even exists. Anyway, just wanted to thank you for a great podcast, I only wish I had the kind of time and resources you have to devote to your show to give to my podcast that I just started (yes, this is a plug coming in for landing!). It's about the college experience on a campus in (literally) the middle of nowhere, Missouri. The first episode was a soundseeing tour of my campus, the second features some clips from a concert I went to featuring a cover band. Check it out if you have 45 mins for the first 2 shows. It's at TruCast and in iTunes; search for TruCast. Thanks and keep up the great work! You are one of the reasons I've started doing my show! Jason Hollowed College Freshman, rookie podcaster, and (if all goes well) Future Music Educator - No iTunes down under - Craig Ashley Russell: Left Field craig@leftfield.com.au to adam More options 2:55 am (13 hours ago) And man, are we pissed off about it. Next time you're taking Jobs, tell him to put a rocket under the record companies. Cause until then, it's Limewire for Aussies, where no one makes a cent! - Fantasy - John Knell john@lightform.net to adam More options Aug 29 (18 hours ago) Hey Adam, Just bought "Fantasy" off of Itunes.... then I remembered how cool "Let's Groove" & "Boogie Wonderland" were and got them at well. So....Earth Wind & Fire got 3 songs downloaded because of the Hit test. Enjoy the Daily Download and keep up the great work. Best regards John Knell - 3K of iTunes! - Nery Orellana nery@swervedesign.com to adam More options Aug 29 (20 hours ago) Hey adam. I can't begin to tell you just how many tunes I've bought after hearing mash-ups and hit tests. I think I've spent in total to date since iTunes launched in canada just over $3000 on albums and audiobooks. It's funny I used to find my music on torrent sites before itunes showed up. And I find myself downloading great oldies versus new releases. PS> love your podcast. Love the whole rss movement and keep up the great work. - Doug Kaye - Doug Kaye to adam More options Aug 29 (21 hours ago) I should be embarrassed to tell you this -- wait, I *AM* embarrassed to tell you -- but after listening to the "Toxic Shack" mashup on the Daily Source Code last week, I went to iTunes and bought Britney Spear's "Toxic." I just wanted to hear the bass line in its original context. Really! Trust me! It was just the bass line. I'll probably never buy another Britney Spears song again, but it's more evidence that mashups do sell music. ...doug Doug Kaye, Executive Producer - 10 cds - Jon Pielaet kd7swh@gmail.com to adam More options Aug 28 (2 days ago) Hi Adam, Just wanted to let you know I have been here since day one of iPodder.org, and will be a lifetime subscriber of the Source Code. Now attending the University of Montana, (Missoula, Montana USA) I volenteered as a technology assistant in my dorm so whenever I go out on a call I tell the residents about podcasting and RSS feeds. It really seems to catch on quickly and everyone is joining "the march". As a side note in reference to your question about mash-ups in episode 229, I have bought at least ten CD's (AAC's worth) as a result of the daily source code. Podcasts can also be great marketing tools if you aren't afraid to put in the effort. If anyone needs an example, look at Rob Costlow. I gave him his first Amazon.com review after hearing him on the show and his amazon sales have surely gone up. In any event, there is no question that "we" can make it ("the march") happen. Best Regards, Jon Pieleat (Pie-lay) Miller Hall at the University of Montana-Missoula - Legal Mashup - Craig Meyer to Adam More options Aug 28 (2 days ago) Adam, You've been doing a great job promoting Indie podcasting. Thanks for all your efforts. I always enjoy the "Daily SourceCode", it makes my commute most enjoyable. I usually arrive at work (or home, depending on when you post) with a smile on my face, and/or quietly giggling to myself. I've been kicking around an idea for reducing bandwidth usage for certain style podcasts. In your recent (#228, 229) podcasts you were talking about MushUps, and something clicked in my head. The quick overview: Generate (assemble) the MashUp on the Users machine. Rather than sending the final MP3 product, send the instructions to a MP3 ReGenerator to build the MashUp from the constituent sound files using a file (stream) of MP3 Assembly instructions. So the User would use iTunes (AllOfMP3.com ;) or existing copies of the MP3 songs, with the MashUp instruction file. A new program would then stitch together the MashUp on their machine and either output to the speakers directly or create an MP3 file for the User to listen to. Assuming the final User has legal copies of the Original music, the MashUp created on their machine is all kosher! This would generate sales of the originals, and avoid RIAA jumping in to kill this new creative art form. It avoids DRM issues, and nicely finesses the "Fair Use" of User's legal copies. This would require creation of two programs: The instruction generator "Compiler", which is used by the MashUp creator. And, the MashUp Assembler engine which would use the instructions to generate the desired MashUp. The instructions would actually be quite simple, involving, selection from the original, and then either straight copying, or blending/mixing with other selections (with optional volume, pitch?, speed?) adjustments. If needed MD5 signatures of the Song originals could be used to verify that the User has the "Correct" version of the song, though this might not always work. Now, given that we have these two applications the Instruction Generator (Compiler) and Assembler. This same idea could be used to reduce the bandwidth usage of certain style podcasts, such as yours! My assumption is that Comcast and other broadband suppliers do some transparent caching of content to avoid always re-fetching common items. And also, that a dedicated listener would have several pre-existing podcasts already on their computer. Since the "Daily SourceCode" is composed of various bits, bumpers, promos. Extend the RSS enclosure to add an optional section. This would build the new podcast from smaller segments, either fetched from the internet (which would hopefully be cached at the broadband suppliers head-end), or optionally as segments copied from known offsets in pre-existing podcasts. I am assuming, that you are using CastBlaster or MegaSeg, with pre-loaded sounds bits to play. I haven't done any analysis, but your shows do have repeated segments. From something as simple as Boing, to the PodShow bumpers, and promos. Now, sometimes you do talk over this segments, (in which case maybe you only send the voice track to mix into the pre-existing segment) This PodCast Assembler idea, all falls apart with something like Dawn and Drew, where there are very few repeated segments. I realize this does a software effort, and also working with the MashUp creative people. I am hoping that CastBlaster's general front- end could be re-used, but replace the MP3 output, with a MP3 Assembler instruction generation module. So, What do you think? Craig Ps. Simplified Example of Assembler instructions Assuming song1.mp3, song2. mp3 and song3.mp3 The Result would mix 23.1 seconds of song1 (at 1/2 volume) with a looped 10 seconds of song2, and with 23.1 seconds of song3 (Pitch increased by 12%) or for the Daily SourceCode, something like: . . . MP3 Licensing - Paul Huff paul.huff@gmail.com to adam More options Aug 29 (17 hours ago) Hey Adam, I'm starting to wonder what's going to happen when the Thomson folks come knocking on the indiecasters doors asking for their minimum royalties of $2000 a year for using mp3s... mp3licensing.com—emd.html As podcasting gets more popular and all the licensing stuff happens with the music, I've been wondering when Thomson is going to try and make itself heard. I have a tiny podcast myself, and have been afraid to do any kind of money-making scheme (advertising, sponsorships, paypal donations, etc.) because I'm afraid of having to pay Thomson anything. Any thoughts? Should we be trying to move away from the mp3 file format? If so, where do we go? Nothing else is as widely supported, it seems... At any rate, keep up the great podcasts... -Paul The New Shownotes - Suck so bad they swallow... - Feedback - Michael Domingues jackfrost.michael@gmail.com to adam More options 2:52 am (13 hours ago) Adam - Regarding my earlier eMail, your new blog format breaks the iTunes description panel as well. Just letting you know (you probably have about 100+ other eMails saying this). Michael Domingues Promo: Mac Gab [Site ] Promo: KZFO Micronational Radio [Site ] BioDiesl Cont... - the real problem with biodiesel and ethanol - Sam Abuelsamid sam@abuelsamid.com to adam More options 1:56 am (14 hours ago) www.theolympian.com—article Adam The problem with these bio-fuels is that if you factor in the energy input in the entire production process, it takes considerably more fossil fuel energy to produce the fuels than you get out of them. This factors in the fuel used by tractors an other equipment and also the refining process itself. "But researchers at Cornell University and the University of California-Berkeley say it takes 29 percent more fossil energy to turn corn into ethanol than the amount of fuel the process produces. For switch grass, a warm weather perennial grass found in the Great Plains and eastern North America United States, it takes 45 percent more energy and for wood, 57percent. It takes 27 percent more energy to turn soybeans into biodiesel fuel and more than double the energy produced is needed to do the same to sunflower plants, the study found." The real answer is to use less energy. sam - Bio Diesel smells like french fries. - James Berghout jamesb@jamesb.com to adam More options Aug 29 (17 hours ago) Adam, The Make Magazine podcast did a 30 minute interview about Bio Diesel. I found it really fascinating. I don't know who is right, but according to the Make magazine podcast, the diesel burning vehicles made today are better suited for Bio Diesel than those made back in the 80's. I also hear that Bio Diesel burning in your fuel tank smells like french fries. James Berghout - Aircraft Diesel - Eric Trytko raoulduke@xsrpms.com to adam More options Aug 29 (18 hours ago) Adam When it comes time to rebuild/replace the engine in the 182RG (BTW you NEED something cooler like a Cirrus SR22 or a Lancair Columbia 400) you might want to consider DeltaHawk Diesel Engines www.deltahawkengines.com which manufactures a diesel motor for the aircraft industry. Duke Dearborn, MI RumbleStripRadio podcast comming SOON! - Cooking Oil - Andy White to adam More options Aug 29 (22 hours ago) Adam, Since you are interested in Bio Diesel, I thought you might find this link of interest, it shows how to make bio diesel from used cooking oil (vegetable oil only). www.freedomfuelamerica.com Andy White -- - Peak Oil - Stephan Segraves s@badice.com to adam More options Aug 28 (2 days ago) Adam, I finally caught up on my listening after a move. The comments by Darren while true have a few things left out. Peak oil is a theory that relies on the assumption that technology will not increase over time. We have come very close to using up known oil resources in the past then a new technology comes along and allows to continue to pumping from wells that would not produce without the technology. People need to understand that oil does not sit in pools underground. It is found in porous rock. The more porous a rock the more oil it holds. The more permeable a rock is the easier the oil flows out of it. With a lot of the new technology we are able to go back to old wells that may have been less permeable and pull out more oil. These technologies include steam flooding, where the well is pumped full of steam and the change in pressure brings the oil and steam substance to the surface. Yes, oil is a finite resource but it is not a predictable finite resource. Five years ago geologists were predicting 35 years of oil left on the face of the Earth, now we are predicting 75-80 yrs. before hitting peak oil. I am all for the use of bio-diesel but it is kind of expensive to produce. There are other technologies as well, such as coal to liquids, which allows us to create gasoline from coal. This is being started in China, www.upi.com—view.cfm and is pretty exciting. Coal is great because there is a huge amount of it and with new drilling laws we can keep The ultimate answer though is to move away from non-renewable energy. The oil companies are scrambling to jump on these things and the company that I worked for (which will remain nameless, though I am sure you can do a search and find it) has started real life experimentation with Hydrogen in Washington D.C. Keep up the great work Adam! -- Stephan Segraves Teenagers cont. - From a teen - Kabren Frostig kabrenlevinson@comcast.net to adam More options 5:00 am (11 hours ago) Hey adam, I heard the source code today, and heard the feedback from an actual teenager, I am a teenager, actually turning 16 soon, so around the same age group. As with a lot of parents, I am an only child by the way, my parents have never experienced a child grow up, let alone a teenager grow up. They seem to have a hard time letting go, at least my mom. I guess its different, since this is feedback from a male teenager, but being a teenager is hard enough with highschool, and friends, espicially being the big geek I am, we don't need any more trouble from parents. Hope this will add to your experience with a teenager. Love the Source code, Kabren (prenounced KAY- bren) - Teen from Belfast - Fra grogan darkchild@gmail.com to adam More options 4:18 am (11 hours ago) Hey Adam, My name is Francis, I'm 15 and from Belfast. Just heard the DSC for the 29th and heard you talk about Mark the surgeon. Last September I was diagnosed with Hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (I fucking DARE YOU to try and say that aloud) or simply HCM. Currently to keep my heart under control I take 1 5mg Beta-Blocker pill a day and I've done the 24 heart monitor thing. Since I always keep on forgetting to ask my doctor, are there any side effects I should expect sometime in the future (even know I've been on beta-blocks for a year) And I do watch MTV, because the simple fact is, I like to look at other people's shallowness (if that's even a word) Cheers. - From a 13 year old - Geoffrey Sneddon geoffers@gmail.com to adam More options 12:11 am (16 hours ago) Hey, I'm a 13 year old boy, and my relationship with my dad is minimal, mainly because he's either dealing with work stuff, or with political stuff - He used to be head of the North East Fife district council, for which he received an OBE. This means he is rarely in the house and not busy. When he is in the house he is often dealing with his 2500+ videos (ergh!). I'm taking you have either been too busy to reply to my previous email, or just been at 100% on Gmail (I'm still at 8MB - 0%!) Umnmmmm... I think that's all... Geoffrey Sneddon. - From a dad - Ben Collins to adam More options 12:05 am (16 hours ago) This past weekend I introduced my son Nick, (13) to the concept of a podcast. We listened to a few that I subscribe to and spent some time talking about what he could do one on. Nick is pretty typically into what most 13 year old boys are, particular video games which he will play as many hours as he can stay awake. He's pretty computer literate and in about half an hour I showed him the basics of Sound Forge and Acid. He sat and worked for about 4 hours straight and designed and created his own podcast; gameSNAFU. At the end of the day he was thrilled with his own efforts and success. For a teenager that is phenomenal concentration and follow through. He spent the rest of the day IM-ing his friends planning new episodes and working on his subscriber base. Wow. As every teenager will tell you, they are smart and insightful. And as any parent will tell you, they need focus, guidance and a creative outlet. Podcasting fits the bill brilliantly. It can be simple or technically sophisticated, meaningful or silly...whatever they want. And it gives them something to do that is active not passive at a time in life when that is really important. Many thanks, Ben Collins Mashup: Imagine This - Wax Audio [Site ] Promo: Yeast Radio [Site ] Feedback PodcastCon UK [Site ] - Via The Tartan Podccast [Site ] Happy Birthday email - David A. Roman David@romanda.org to adam More options 12:12 pm (3½ hours ago) Its so wild your birthday is 9/3/64.. Lets see why. 1. My Brother's birthday is 9/3/55 2. My Son's Birthday is 9/3/95 3. My birthday is 11/20/64 I wanted to tell you Happy Birthday and Keep the DSC coming!!! My Brother and I work together for a company that sells and maintains the control systems for about 50% of the power plants in the USA. He turned me onto podcasts in January and the first 2 weeks we were in FLA on a job site, we car-pooled into the plant and listened to you every day. It was really a great time. We LOVE 'da hit test, it’s a blast. We both have iPods and have so many podcasts on them we cant listen to them all. I look forward to the DSC more then any of the others, it is still by far the best. Mark (my brother)'s son just started College and My son Just started 5th grade, and listening to you with Christiana is a blast. The new line for the office is "This sucks so bad it swallows" - you can tell Christiana thanks for that one. I about wrecked my car driving home listening to that podcast. KEEP UP THE GRRRREEEEAAATTT WORK! Podcasts have changed the way I listen to the world. Lybia, Syria? - Mark Fonseca Rendeiro to Adam More options 8:53 am (7 hours ago) Hey Adam.. greetings from the 'dam. Since timewise Im ahead of the states, I figure Ill be among the first to send one of those typical email-dsc-corrections. Lockerbie... the Pan-Am bombing.. has been linked to Libya. And yes.. Qadhafi has accepted responsibility for it.. the nation has also agreed to pay financial compensation to each family. Couple of million per person. Actually its a great example of how to diplomatically engage a country with a controversial leader.. instead of this invade and occupy stuff... these days Qadhafi is really obsessed with his legacy and his image home and abroad.. so he's finally cooperating with the international community. We could have done the same to saddam... instead of isolating.. engage.. eventually (slowly) changes do occur. Anyway long-winded correction. Take care. -- -bicycleMark PodSafe: Cruisebox - Heard it on a Podcast [Site ] - PodSafe Music Network [Site ] Hit Test #53 [Site ]

Geoff Garside ggarside@gmail.com to adam More options Aug 28 (1 day ago) Hi Adam, I just listened to your August 24th podcast and thought I would share with your my experience of my British Airways flight from Moscow. Due to the strike of Gate Gourmet there was to be no food on the flight. However while the plane was being refueled and so on the stewards and stewardesses had gone out and purchased some food for the passengers. Each passenger was then given a bag of food and so on as they boarded the plane. In the bag was an apple, banana, can of pepsi, sandwich, mars bar. Personally I thought this was the best selection of food I had ever had on any flight anywhere, it was also much nicer to be able to eat as and when I felt like it rather than in the slice of time when they have put the food in front of me. Happy birthday for you and your daughter, Geoff

GPS Accuracy
DSC #229 GPS
Pilot Mike to adam More options Aug 27 (2 days ago) Adam, Thanks! We'll work on a Pilotcast promo for you. I'm listening to DSC #229. You should know the Selective Availabilty dithering for the GPS signal has been gone since its removal was ordered by President Clinton in 2000. SA hasn't even been restored in war time. We suspect that the government has more tricks so SA isn't needed. www.ngs.noaa.gov—sans_SA We know that the govmint retains the right to restore SA and kill GPS in its entirety in case of emergency. There was a rumor, from supposed knowledgeable CFIs, that VORs and other navaids were turned off on 9/11 but when I brought it up online we found out that wasn't true. There is a competing GPS system called GALILEO being setup by the by EU specifically so they have a system where the USA doesn't have the OFF switch. europa.eu.int—index_en.htm The other GPS system is WAAS (Wide Area Augmentation System) and local WAAS where ground-based GPS transmitters and repeaters are being installed to get the kind of precision needed for precision approaches. AOPA President Phil Boyer demonstrated using a new WAAS approach at Frederick, MD, comparing it to ILS and it was amazing. You'll hear from us on the demo shortly! Thanks again. --"Pilot Mike" The Pilotcast www.pilotcast.com
GPS selective availability
Greg Grusby greg@thoughtagency.com to adam More options Aug 26 (3 days ago) Adam, After listening to Friday's show I thought this site on GPS might interest you: tinyurl.com—cgd3u The news goes back to 2000 but it speaks to your point on the removal of selective availability built into the GPS system. Then again, when our government gives us something it usually means they have something much, much, more advanced that they've created in a lab that 'doesn't exist.' No worries, even if somebody managed to find out about it, the government would neither confirm nor deny its existence. And, by the way I have purchased original-back catalog tracks after hearing remixes/mash-ups on Daily Source Code. I'd rather buy my music on ITMS then anyplace else. Keep up the fantastic work. Staying subscribed, -Greg
Selective Availability
rjolivier@mac.com to adam More options Aug 26 (3 days ago) Robert in Los Angeles [1] sent this email to you through the Radio UserLand [2] community server, re this page [3]. Adam, I work with GPS on cell phones all day and I can tell you that your listener that said commercial GPS is less accurate that military GPS due to induced errors is BS. It was called Selective Availability and it was turned off in May, 2000. A commercial GPS with a good stable clock and a good antenna design is accurate to better than 5 meters. Military GPS is better becasue the GPS satellites actually transmit data on two frequencies, only one of which is available to commecial GPS receivers. Military units listen on both frequencies. The reason for this is that the a large source of error is caused by ionospheric interferences in the atmosphere. The ionosphere causes slight delay in the signal reaching earth but this delay is inversely proportional to the frequency of the signal. Hence, by using two frequencies, a military receiver can detect the ionospheric delay difference between the two frequencies and cancel it leading to mugh higher accuracy. Additionally, bombs are moving entities. The last source of GPS error is called multipath reflection where the GPS signal bounces off of objects and causes the receiver to see duplicates of the signal delayed by various amounts of time. This happens mostly in urban environments where the signal bounces off of tall buildings. A moving GPS receiver is able to see the difference in the multipath characteristics as it is moving through the terrain and create a model that cancels out most of them where a stationary unit cannot. Since a bomb is definitely moving, it is able to cancel the multipath out with great accuracy. These two factors are soley responsible for why a smart bomb is so accurate, not induced errors. Check the wikipedia ... en.wikipedia.org—Selective_availability Peace out. robert
"PODCAST FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS"
wichitarutherford@mac.com to WichitaRutherf. More options 12:54 am (12 hours ago) Hi everybody. Wichita Rutherford here. Why don't we do this as the podcasting community. Let's all do 2 to 3 minute podcasts that will inspire people to give to the Red Cross or food banks or whatever organization they choose to help these folks who are gonna be without food, water, shelter, clothing, medicine and Lord knows what all else. This thing could get ugly quick. So if we went ahead and prepared, we'd be ready to do what we do best to help them. We have a big infrastructure now with millions of listeners, let's put ourselves and our podcasts to the side for a minute and put links to these organizations (whichever ones you choose) as the main focus and links on our sites. I mean on the front page too. There are lots of us now and I think we've got enough ears listening that might help make a difference to these people. Let's keep it simple and call it "PODCASTING FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS". Let's not have a site to go to or anything for it, let's just put that phrase on our sites, and send listeners on to where they can help. In a nutshell it would look like this: I'M PODCASTING FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS. Please help by donating your time/money/assistance to one of the following organizations: LINK - LINK - LINK Even a little will help a lot. Thank you so much _______. Then do a short 1 to 2 minute podcast asking folks to help the same way. No joking around, no bad language. Just as serious as you can get with your delivery. Thank them, then sign off. Or send a copy of it to me if you want and I'll put it on the "PODCAST FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS" Podcast. Or do both. The first one goes up tonight. (Sunday) Let's do this as the podcasting community. Let's show how powerful this medium actually is. This goes for the directories too. PodcastAlley.com PodcastDirectory.com PodcastPickle.com ALL of you in charge of podcast directories. Pass this on to your podcast host connections, send it to everyone you know who does a podcast. Professional or beginner. iTunes and Disney as well as your cousin in Toledo who's only done 2 shows. Don't even email me back, just get started forwarding this message. Let's get ready to help these people. They're gonna need it. Let's PODCAST FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS. Podcasting for hurricane victims, your pal, Wichita 5MinutesWithWichita.com
Teenagers
Caroline caroline@jedimaster.smith.edu to adam More options Aug 27 (2 days ago) Ahoy Adam. In the DSC today you mentioned that you hadn't gotten any feedback from teenagers... So here you go. I'm about the same age as Christina (turning 15 in a couple months) and, speaking as a teenage girl (and oldest child), I can tell you that fathers are no picnic either. Your relationship with her actually reminds me a lot of mine with my dad and, although I love him dearly, he's a hassle. My parents haven't experienced a child grow up before, and it seems to be harder for them to let go of me than for me to renounce them. Go figure. Also worth mentioning, I think, is that (in my case) much of the insolence and rebellion is calculated. We teenagers are smarter than you think. After 15 years of living under the rule of parents, we have learned how to manipulate, placate, and annoy you in ways that I don't think you understand. Or maybe my parents are just easy. Whatever the reason, I think that us capable, intelligent teenage girls are vastly underrated. I don't really know what Christina is like, but I would bet that she has things much more under control than you believe. Thanks for your great podcast, if not for your love of teenagers. =) - Caroline

From listening to your show I discovered this product and so last weekend I took my cash down to a local department store and got one. And here in Australia the pods work out at about 33 cents each so it's cheaper in the long run than getting takeway coffees from a cafe. The dark roast pack is quickly becomming my favourite. Bar stool recommendation + your new equipment broke my ipod!
Graeme Shaw GraemeShaw@bigfoot.com to adam More options Aug 28 (1 day ago) Adam, Loving the DSC, keep up the good work. Thought I'd recommend a bar stool to you, my Dad has a Bombo Bar stool. They look very stylish, you can adjust the height, and they're incredibly comfortable. John Lewis seem to be one of the cheapest places to buy them, their page is here: www.johnlewis.com—Stools 230176394/Product.aspx On a slightly different note, I was sitting having my lunch time coffee in a coffee shop, listening to the DSC at the beginning of the week when you first mentioned your new audio equipment. Literally as you said "it's a Monday, so shit's going to break" the audio went dead. I just thought it was you pissing about, but when I looked down, I noticed my ipod had turned itself off. I pressed the play button and it turned back on, pressed it again, and it resumed playing the DSC! So your new equipment temporarily killed my ipod! I'm sure you'll pleased to know that it's been fine since. As I said, keep up the good work! Cheers, Graeme
IRAQ
Brian Shirey subrolex@sssnet.com to adam More options Aug 27 (2 days ago) Mr. Curry: Love the DSC! I got turned on to Ipod when stationed in Iraq. Just heard the August 16th show. Your views about the Iraqi people are right on target. I was stationed at ABU GHRAIB, (after the scandal broke, thank you) and most of the Deatinee (prisoner) population weren't Iraqi. Mostly they were Syrian. After all how can a group of insergents gallavant across the country unfunded? The Iraqi people are SO poor that they couldn't fund this type of terrorism. My thought is that the Syrian government is afraid. They are think first Iraq, then us. Syrian culture is economically, politicalily and religiously mirror that of Iraq. Just my two cents, that's all. Love the Daily Source Code, I remember you from back in the days when MTV actually played music videos! Brian

Bio Diesel
NO BIODIESEL, PLEASE
Jürgen Schlund juergen.schlund@vr-web.de to adam More options Aug 28 (16 hours ago) Hi Adam, in your last DSC you mentioned to buy a Diesel and use Biodiesel. DONt DO THAT, allthough its cheaper than "normal" Diesel Why ? Ok, I try to explain. Biodiesel is a synthetic product, made out of Rapeseed and Methanol. Allthough the molecular structure is very similar to Diesel, it may damage your engine. Diesel fuel made out of oil has a lot of lubrication capabilities for the special Injection and Pump parts of a diesel engine. The use of Biodiesel does not garantee the lubrication of these parts. In addition, Biodiesel is very, very aggressive to the small fuel pipelines and rupper parts in your engine, which have contact with the fuel. This is the reason why BMW Diesel cars need a special Biodiesel kit when using Biodiesel fuel. Volkswagen does not approve their current Diesels for Biodiesel, the old ones are approved. There is a huge german Diesel-Community on the Internet, where these topics are discussed very contrary, but most of the people agree to my opinion, that it is not worth saving 10 or 15 ct for a liter of biodiesel when you need to spend 1.500 Euro for the repairing of your Diesel injection system. Hope that helps Keep on rocking with DSC!! Greetings from Bavaria, Germany Juergen ... driving a Volkswagen TDI with 195.000 km, first engine, first injection pump and NO Biodiesel ;-)
Forget biodiesel - check out bioHEAT!
Christopher S. Penn cspenn@gmail.com to adam More options Aug 26 (3 days ago) Bioheat - the use of biodiesel fuel for home heating... eliminating another avenue of fossil fuels... www.boston.com—bioheat_gaining_steam_as_home_heating_option Rock on! -- Christopher S. Penn

Purchase after hit test
Marc Katz mkatz@heartsurgeryva.com to adam More options 3:22 am (9 hours ago) Adam, In answer to your question, I frequently purchase songs on iTunes after having heard them on DSC and the Hit Test. It is great to hear that music and the memories it rekindles. Congratulations on the success you are having with Podcasting. I have been listening since the beginning of the year and am hooked. I rarely ever turn on the radio anymore. I am a heart surgeon in Richmond, Virginia, and am likely older than your average listener. If I can be of assistance from the stand point of medical information (I also work in transplantation and surgical robotics) in your continued progress promoting podcasting please feel free to contact me. Keep up the great work, Marc -- Marc R. Katz MD Chief of Cardiac Surgery Henrico Doctors’ Hospital Virginia Transplant Center
EWF Fantasy bought!
Antonio M. Rosario antonio@amrosario.com to adam More options 12:39 am (12 hours ago) Adam, I thought I'd let you know that after listening to the Hit Test on your last podcast, I, too , went to the iTunes Music store and bought EW&F's song Fantasy. While I was there I picked up 4 more of their songs that I was surprised I did not have in my collection yet. So, hell yeah, the Hit Test sells songs! Antonio Portfolio - www.amrosario.com Blog - amrpix.blogspot.com "Time flies like an arrow. Fruit Flies like a banana." Groucho Marx
Music purchased from mashups
David Sheaffer sheaffer@sac.sticare.com to adam More options Aug 28 (19 hours ago) Adam, I've purchased four songs from itunes after hearing them in mashups. You're right, it's a great way to promote back catalog. ie: I hadn't thought about 'Rock Steady' by Aretha Franklin for years, heard a snippet in a mashup, went to itunes, downlaoded it, dragged it to my ipod, done. BTW, if you haven't already, you have to listen to this episode of Chub Creek. They do a great sendup of the source code and it and the skit surrounding it are the funniest stuff I've heard in a podcast. I actually had to turn off my ipod to breathe. It's at the beginning and it's only about 5 minutes. homepage.mac.com—index.html episode 'chub creek not' from August 5th. Thanks for all the great work promoting this method of getting content that isn't available anywhere else. I really haven't listened to commercial radio for about 6 months now and, when I have to, I hate it even more than I used to. Leo Laporte was on our local NPR station here in Sacramento last week discussing podcasting and he made a great point. When you're home in the evening you have lots of audio/video equipment competing for your time but podcasts can be enjoyed while you're doing things like gardening, riding your bike, running, putting away the dishes, etc. I've done all of those activities while listening and that's so true. Thanks again, Dave Sheaffer
Purchasing music heard on DSC / People Downloading via Dialup
Kevin Crossman kevin@kevdo.com to adam More options Aug 27 (2 days ago) Yep. Purchased two Rob Costlow tracks and Stevie Wonder's Superstition ("Bootystition"). I also download lots of mashup and podsafe tracks you play. You know... the kind of stuff you can't purchase even if you wanted to. Would happily happily happily purchase mashups if I could! Have heard from a relatively high percentage of my listeners and they are downloading via a dialup connection! It takes them an hour to download my show, which is incredible since we've got a really "narrow interest" show and we're not exactly the most produced. But it does show how motivated folks can be about the topics they love. -Kevin Kevin Crossman, The Frat Pack Tribute Stiller, Vaughn, Ferrell, Wilson, Wilson www.the-frat-pack.com Listen to our Podcast, www.fratpackpodcast.com www.the-frat-pack.com—FPT-Promo-1min-Aug2005.mp3
buying music after hearing it
Brett Rann brett@breesestreet.org to adam More options Aug 27 (2 days ago) I certainly go looking for it after I hear it on your show! Unfortunately I'm in australia and we don't have much option for buying music online -- i think there' s a couple but it's windows media player drm stuff and we're a 100% mac house. I'd much rather pay $1-$2 than spend half an hour digging through the scum of p2p and cleverly crafted google searches to find a song. I'm currently looking for earth wind and fire fantasy... love that song! Found "groove tonight" here mp3.jet2web.net—data online_classics/dance_classics1/, which is ok, but I'd much rather fantasy. This is after about 15 minutes of searching. Who knows how much longer before I can find Fantasy. Half an hour of my time is worth much more than $1-2 freaking dollars. C'est la vie! At least Apple is on the case. A few friends use www.allofmp3.com which I think is some russian site that offers music downloads for unbelievably low prices, and apparently don't really pass on any royalties. I'd rather get it for free than give them some $ ! It's insane that the only way I can get my music easily is to either order a CD online and wait a few days for delivery, or make a trip to the city and cross my fingers that they have the album I'm after. Keep that podsafe stuff coming through! Brett -- software developer in melbourne, australia.
hit test drives track sales
frank herfs frankherfs@gmail.com to adam More options Aug 26 (3 days ago) Hello Adam, referring to the Hit Test drive track sales question, yes I have bought a lot of music from itunes after listening the daily source code. The main reason that I did it after a hit test and not years before is simple. I didn´t know the name of the band or the song. Jan plays a lot of great songs of the 70th. The time when I grow up. I have always liked this music but was too young to keep in mind the artists when they were at the crest of their fame. 30 years later I hear these great songs again. But today there is a big difference: you and jan can tell everyone from whom the music is which is fantastic. With this knowledge itunes helps me to find what i am looking for and usually it takes only a few minutes until the song is mine. Thank god for podcasting. Frank -- www.fherfs.blogspot.com
