Staying subscribed, -Greg - Selective Availability - rjolivier@mac.com to adam More options Aug 26 (3 days ago) Robert in Los Angeles [1] sent this email to you through the Radio UserLand [2] community server, re this page [3]. Adam, I work with GPS on cell phones all day and I can tell you that your listener that said commercial GPS is less accurate that military GPS due to induced errors is BS. It was called Selective Availability and it was turned off in May, 2000. A commercial GPS with a good stable clock and a good antenna design is accurate to better than 5 meters. Military GPS is better becasue the GPS satellites actually transmit data on two frequencies, only one of which is available to commecial GPS receivers. Military units listen on both frequencies. The reason for this is that the a large source of error is caused by ionospheric interferences in the atmosphere. The ionosphere causes slight delay in the signal reaching earth but this delay is inversely proportional to the frequency of the signal. Hence, by using two frequencies, a military receiver can detect the ionospheric delay difference between the two frequencies and cancel it leading to mugh higher accuracy. Additionally, bombs are moving entities. The last source of GPS error is called multipath reflection where the GPS signal bounces off of objects and causes the receiver to see duplicates of the signal delayed by various amounts of time. This happens mostly in urban environments where the signal bounces off of tall buildings. A moving GPS receiver is able to see the difference in the multipath characteristics as it is moving through the terrain and create a model that cancels out most of them where a stationary unit cannot. Since a bomb is definitely moving, it is able to cancel the multipath out with great accuracy. These two factors are soley responsible for why a smart bomb is so accurate, not induced errors. Check the wikipedia ... en.wikipedia.org—Selective_availability Peace out. robert "PODCAST FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS" - wichitarutherford@mac.com to WichitaRutherf. Let's all do 2 to 3 minute podcasts that will inspire people to give to the Red Cross or food banks or whatever organization they choose to help these folks who are gonna be without food, water, shelter, clothing, medicine and Lord knows what all else. This thing could get ugly quick. So if we went ahead and prepared, we'd be ready to do what we do best to help them. We have a big infrastructure now with millions of listeners, let's put ourselves and our podcasts to the side for a minute and put links to these organizations (whichever ones you choose) as the main focus and links on our sites. I mean on the front page too. There are lots of us now and I think we've got enough ears listening that might help make a difference to these people. Let's keep it simple and call it "PODCASTING FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS". Let's not have a site to go to or anything for it, let's just put that phrase on our sites, and send listeners on to where they can help. In a nutshell it would look like this: I'M PODCASTING FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS. Please help by donating your time/money/assistance to one of the following organizations: LINK - LINK - LINK Even a little will help a lot. Thank you so much _______. Then do a short 1 to 2 minute podcast asking folks to help the same way. No joking around, no bad language. Just as serious as you can get with your delivery. Thank them, then sign off. Or send a copy of it to me if you want and I'll put it on the "PODCAST FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS" Podcast. Or do both. The first one goes up tonight. (Sunday) Let's do this as the podcasting community. Let's show how powerful this medium actually is. This goes for the directories too. PodcastAlley.com PodcastDirectory.com PodcastPickle.com ALL of you in charge of podcast directories. Pass this on to your podcast host connections, send it to everyone you know who does a podcast. Professional or beginner. iTunes and Disney as well as your cousin in Toledo who's only done 2 shows. Don't even email me back, just get started forwarding this message. Let's get ready to help these people. They're gonna need it. Let's PODCAST FOR HURRICANE VICTIMS. In the DSC today you mentioned that you hadn't gotten any feedback from teenagers... So here you go. I'm about the same age as Christina (turning 15 in a couple months) and, speaking as a teenage girl (and oldest child), I can tell you that fathers are no picnic either. Your relationship with her actually reminds me a lot of mine with my dad and, although I love him dearly, he's a hassle. My parents haven't experienced a child grow up before, and it seems to be harder for them to let go of me than for me to renounce them. Go figure. Also worth mentioning, I think, is that (in my case) much of the insolence and rebellion is calculated. We teenagers are smarter than you think. After 15 years of living under the rule of parents, we have learned how to manipulate, placate, and annoy you in ways that I don't think you understand. Or maybe my parents are just easy. Whatever the reason, I think that us capable, intelligent teenage girls are vastly underrated. I don't really know what Christina is like, but I would bet that she has things much more under control than you believe. DONt DO THAT, allthough its cheaper than "normal" Diesel Why ? Ok, I try to explain. Biodiesel is a synthetic product, made out of Rapeseed and Methanol. Allthough the molecular structure is very similar to Diesel, it may damage your engine. Diesel fuel made out of oil has a lot of lubrication capabilities for the special Injection and Pump parts of a diesel engine. The use of Biodiesel does not garantee the lubrication of these parts. In addition, Biodiesel is very, very aggressive to the small fuel pipelines and rupper parts in your engine, which have contact with the fuel. This is the reason why BMW Diesel cars need a special Biodiesel kit when using Biodiesel fuel. Volkswagen does not approve their current Diesels for Biodiesel, the old ones are approved. There is a huge german Diesel-Community on the Internet, where these topics are discussed very contrary, but most of the people agree to my opinion, that it is not worth saving 10 or 15 ct for a liter of biodiesel when you need to spend 1.500 Euro for the repairing of your Diesel injection system. Hope that helps Keep on rocking with DSC!! item.title: Podshow on Sirius PSS-2005-05-19-2
item.itunes:title: Podshow on Sirius PSS-2005-05-19-2
item.dc:creator: Adam Curry
item.description:
I've been receiving lots of email, submissions and requests for and about the Podshow on Sirius. We're in our first full week and P-Dub and I have worked out most of the kinks in the production system. Quite a lot of bits to look after as it pertains to what airs when,
rotation and repeats. Most of this is automated, but there's still a
fair amount of good old fashioned scheduling done by hand/ear. What's interesting is that my Daily Source Code
showprep now comes from the podcasts that are on the Podshow, I always
listened to a lot of podcasts, that number seems to have tripled! What's really working well are the promos podcasters are sending in. The podsafe music submissions are heating up as well. Unlike a personality based radio show, this program is completely
filled daily with podcasts, promos, podsafe music and mashups. I'm
there to tie all the elements together. Much like DSC, only much less
Adam :) The daily shownotes are still a problem, first of all we're working on
converting logs from our playout system, secondly and most important, is
the lack of good information in the ID3 tags.
The better use we make of them, the easier it will be for those 'just
tuning in' to find the podcast they heard online and subscribe. Once we
see more mp3's with full ID3 tags, we can start utilizing RDS
capabilities, so your podcast url can be seen on the display of the
satellite receiver. Here's a link to the second hour as it will be broadcast today. Shownotes: 1. Stickit 2. Pocast_Open 3. Mashup: Another one by DJ BC called "Teach" it features Crosby Stills & Nash vs. Tony Rebel http://www.djbc.net 4. The Riddle 5. Promo Time 6. Promo: Voices From The Vault promo 7. Safety Council Message 8. Podsafe: "Porcupine" by the Falling Wallendas - "Considered by some rock critics to be one of the best unsung alternapop bands in the country. They have a reputation for being strangely beautiful and, well, just strange." another garageband.com band. 9. Podsafe: "Adrenaline" by Nick Johansen - "Nick Johansen is a singer/songwriter from Ottawa, Canada. He has just finished his upcoming release produced by Leslie Howe for Mad Cow Music, and he and his band are playing local venues and gearing up for showcases to record labels.
http://www.nicolasjohansen.com<;;wbr>/main.htm 10. Podsafe: "Everywhere I Go" by Buffygirl - Buffy is a Boston-based singer songwriter. She's still working on her first CD. If the rest of it is as tight as this song it will be well worth buying. Sort of a laid back funky groove.
http://www.buffygirl.com/ 11. Podcast_Sweep09_05_16 12. Podcast: "Family Reviews" This show they review the Lemony Snicket
movie. 13. Podcast: "The Catholic Insider" Part one of his Star Wars
Chronicles. 14. Podcast: "Podcheck Weekly Review" - Scott Fletcher reviews the prior
weeks podcasting news. Submit yer stuff:submit[at]podshow.compodsafe[at]podshow.commashup[at]podshow.com

item.title: Daily Source Code for Friday April 08th 2005
item.itunes:title: Daily Source Code for Friday April 08th 2005
item.dc:creator: Adam Curry
item.description:
Another beta-cast of the CastBlaster Software. This show still has some
bugs in it, but much better than yesterday. I need to do a better job
of watching my levels when not using the 'auto' feature, so the sound
is a bit 'hot' now and then. But again, it's beta :) My father in law jumped into the mix by building me a mini sound-dimmer
so I can use my normal microphone on the input of the tablet. Pictures
here. Today also featured a skype call with Christina to demonstrate that integration. Overall I'm really jazzed! Over the weekend I'm sure I'll be doing more testing. mp3 Duration: 00:27:21
item.itunes:author: Adam Curry
item.itunes:summary:
Another beta-cast of theCastBlasterSoftware. This show still has some bugs in it, but much better than yesterday. I need to do a better job of watching my levels when not using the 'auto' feature, so the sound is a bit 'hot' now and then. But again, it's beta :)
My father in law jumped into the mix by building me a mini sound-dimmer so I can use my normal microphone on the input of the tablet. Pictures .
Today also featured a skype call with Christina to demonstrate that integration. Overall I'm really jazzed!
Over the weekend I'm sure I'll be doing more testing.

item.itunes:title: Daily Source Code for Thursday March 24th 2005
item.dc:creator: Adam Curry
item.description: Show details Podcast on March 24th 2005 From Curry Cottage, Guildford UK Direct download link Podcast feed Weblog Email MP3 Submissions and feedback your dj has just begun No Stinkin' Transmitters Adam's Podcasting Sweeper Rockmaninov Opener Mountain - Mississippi Queen dan novatnak one man revolution 15 second promo About promos Mashups client side email Michael Ridley Hey Adam- Been listening to the Daily Source Code for a few months. Very much enjoy the program. I enjoy the mashups that you play, as it's always fun to hear new and creative things. As you know, there are some legality issues surrounding making and distributing mashups since the mashup producer does not typically get the sampling and redistribution rights to the original music. One idea that has been thrown around on the pho list (http://www.pholist.org) for quite a while is client-side mixing of mashups. As far as I know it's still just an idea and I'm not aware of any software that actually does it. But I think it's an interesting idea and who knows- maybe it will take off one of these years. The general idea is that instead of the producer releasing the actual finished product of their remix (in mp3, CD format, whatever), they would use some tool (presumably something that works similar to Sony's Acid or the other remixing tools out there) to do the mix. But then they would distribute the mix as instructions - data - to be input by a client side tool. The listener would already have to have the constituent songs that make up the mix (presumably loops, samples, etc. would be distributed with the mix instructions). The client side tool would read the mixing instructions and render the mix output on the fly. In this model, the producer doesn't have to (potentially illegally) redistribute any of the source songs. It would be up to the listener to already have copies of the songs. Again, as far as I know this is just a concept that has been floating around for a while. I'm not familiar with any tools that actually DO this on the production or listening side, or of any standards for it. But I have always thought it was a creative solution to the copyright problem. Anyway, thanks for the great program. Keep up the good work! -m http://www.secretelite.com/michael Airport security email Wayne Pittenger Dear Adam, Got an interesting story about the state of airport security. My wife's friend visited us in Pennsylvania from Florida. Before she flew up here, she packed duffel with about 80 plastic easter eggs packed with various prizes for an easter egg hunt. Her husband had warned her that she might not get through security with a duffel full of easter eggs. In spite of that, she went through airport security and the flight north without as much as a search through the duffel. She still had to have her shoes checked though. Regards, Wayne Pittenger www.techntunes.blogspot.com Podcast at 37000 feet email Chris Stork You were my sitter in the 80's when i told the folks I was too sick for school. The bummer though is my 24 year old wife listens to the DSC and says, "Adam who?" Since it sounds you are an aviation buff - thought you'd like this. I'm a captain on an ERJ-145 for a U.S. regional airline. I plug my ipod into the observer audiopanel and listen to the daily sourcecode on long flights at 37,000 feet. You come in through our headphones and keep us entertained like The Lone Ranger did for our folks. With 16 million dollars of airplane strapped to my ass and next generation radiocontent in my ears I like to think i'm flying into the future. As the sun set last night we were ontop a thin layer of clouds around flight level 350. When the last wisp of light fell under the deck and the stars popped out above it was as if we were on the edge of the atmosphere. For a second - we were major tom and you ground control. Unfortunately, as I enjoyed that moment, my flight attendant called up to say some dude was yacking in the aisle. Thanks for keeping us smiling up at altitude. Good luck in your flight training. Hope to see you on a flight. I had Foghat on a flight once off to a gig at the Dayton Ohio Civic Center. They've come along way. I made the PA to the back about the weather and what have you. I ended by saying, "It's been a slow ride - so take it easy." They got off, looked up and gave us the three fingered "You're a rockstar" salute. Chris Stork Mike Montalvo Soundscape Mike's Lifecast Fat Matt The Fat Matt Show Promo Fat Matt Show Pomo 1 About a business model THNK then Podshow now Robert Nelson Duration: 00:33:31

item.description: Show details Podcast on March 16th 2005 From Curry Cottage, Guildford UK Direct download link Podcast feed Weblog Email MP3 Submissions and feedback DSC Don't wanna fuck with No Stinkin' Transmitters Adam's Podcasting Sweeper Rockmaninov Opener Adam's groove mix email Hey Adam, With your years of experience, you've got a natural rhythm. So, I spent a couple hours in front of ACID Studio and put it to music: Openpodcast #1344 http://openpodcast.org/media/2005/3/15/openpodcast_1344.mp3 Some of the clips that I chose aren't necessarily the most flattering, but I did it with love. I remember the worst thing about being in radio was when the Production Manager sat me down to go over my aircheck each week. He pointed out ALL of my stumbles and bumbles, but I always thought those bumbles were part of my charm. There is an enormous amount of character and truth in those moments of verbal indecision, and that's one of the reasons why I like listening to podcasts so much; Most podcasters haven't had the innocence beaten out of them by the broadcast establishment. Keep up the great work, and good luck with Boku. --Scott Fletcher Scott Fletcher OpenPodcast.org Adam's Groove Mix - OpenPodcast.org #1348 MJ doug's question Doug Ritter to adam More options Mar 15 (11 hours ago) Let's step into the time machine and pretend Christina was actually born Christopher. Would you let Christopher stay at Michael Jackson's house? Love the show, Doug in Philadelphia -- Sent from my Treo Blip at beginning Buzz in mic Jo'El Benge www.nogagreflex.com Duration: 00:37:45

item.description: Show details Podcast on February 28th 2005 From Curry Cottage, Guildford UK Direct download link Podcast feed Weblog Email MP3 Submissions and feedback Adam's Podcasting Sweeper Rockmaninov Opener Dan Klass (@ The Bitterest Pill) www.thebitterestpill.com 2005 The Year Of Podcasting Pimp Daddy Sid'd mashups email Yoh Curry, Here's another track to kickstart this new week. Heard on the DSC that people ask you where you get your Mash Ups. As a collector I can show you and your listeners some cool sites that you can link on your weblog so people could explore the wonderfull world of Mash Ups themselfs. No worries, the specials ones are really hard to find so there's enough for the DSC. This track was made by Pheugoo. One of the best in his kind and also one of my personal favorites. This is a mash between Jackson and Therapy?. The're many mases of 'I want you back' and this is one of the best I know. You can find more stuff from at www.pheugoo.nl. Enjoy it. Sidhappens Pheugoo Jackson Family Therapy? beatallica petition http://www.petitiononline.com/p1gp0g/petition.html Brick House cadence from P-Dub P.W. Fenton Digital Flotsam Radio Free Radio - Digital Flotsam 07.5 iPodder.org Catholic Insider ci20050227 Mike Corley mashups email Hey Adam, Since you didn't actually mention it on the show, and everyone may not know, NDA stands for Non-Disclosure Agreement--which pretty much translates to No Damn Announcements anyway. Yes I do remember Veruca Salt. In fact, that leads right into the first track I have for you. After Veruca Salt disbanded, Nina Gordon went on to a solo career--much mure mellow then what you might remember from Veruca Salt, but good nontheless. She also recorded a cover song, of the classic NWA hit -- Straight outta Compton. http://mywebpages.comcast.net/onyxfrog/mp3/StraightOutOfCompton.mp3 Now Adam, I know I haven't sent you one in a while, but I have sent you mashups before. So I'll just assume that when you said that you get all of yours from Cid that you mean "Cid and that Mike Corley." Ok, well to get back on your good side here is one of my favorite mashups as of late. Its by Dinbot (http://www.dinbot.com) and is quite well molded. The first artist is 50 Cent, hard ass gangsta who's been shot (nine times!,) stabbed, arrested, you name it, fiddys done it. Now what can match the hardness of this rock of pure gangsta? Nothing short of Devo with Whip It. Obviously. Check it out, its called Whipsta! http://mywebpages.comcast.net/onyxfrog/mp3/Whipsta-Devovs.50Cent.mp3 One last thing for ya. I did this a while ago and the plan was to get it put on a t-shirt butthast never happened so I'll send it to you to do waht you want with it. http://mywebpages.comcast.net/onyxfrog/img/podfather.gif Ok, Adam, I'll talk to you soon and I'll make sure that you have someone else to get you mashups. -Mike Corley dINbOT www.dinbot.com Whipsta (Devo vs. 50 Cent) Break MegaSeg House Cold Jan Polet Jan Polet's Hit Test Hit Test 16 Podsafe Steven Alvarado/The Howl Sessions Duration: 00:44:24

item.description: Show details Podcast on February 25th 2005 From San Francisco, California Direct download link Podcast feed Weblog Email MP3 Submissions and feedback No Stinkin' Transmitters - OpenPodcast.org #554 5th generation of RnR Adam's Podcasting Sweeper Rockmaninov Opener Veruca Salt vs Yazoo Don't seether Aluminium email from scott ALUMINIUM VERSUS ALUMINUM I thought this was funny, because I had this argument with a friend of mine before. You said : "'aluminium', which is the correct pronunciation - that's not actually an alloy" First of all, an 'alloy' is a compound of two or more metals. Aluminum (or Aluminium) is a pure element, not an alloy. The metal was named by the English chemist Sir Humphry Davy, who derived the name from the mineral called alumina. Sir Humphry first spelled it alumium in 1807, then changed it to aluminum, and finally settled on aluminium in 1812. English chemists liked the latter, because it sounds like many other elements whose names end in -ium, like magnesium, potassium, and sodium. The American Chemical Society adopted the -um spelling in 1925, and the International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC) officially standardised on 'aluminium' in 1990. In 1993, however, IUPAC recognized 'aluminum' as an acceptable variant. Most American chemistry papers still use 'Aluminum', not 'Aluminium'. These are big smart people with PhD's. http://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=aluminum&ie=UTF-8&oe=UTF-8&hl=en&btnG=Search http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aluminum#Spelling In the end, the Merriam-Webster dictionary spells and pronounces it 'Aluminum', and states 'Aluminium' as an British derivative. The Oxford English Dictionary has both as acceptable spellings. http://www.m-w.com/mw/table/element.htm http://www.m-w.com/cgi-bin/dictionary?book=Dictionary&va=aluminum Just thought I'd help out, in case some limey Brit is trying to make you think that your perfectly acceptable American pronunciation is inferior. The next time someone says "it's really 'aluminium'", feel free to respond with "you commie". Scott Chacon http://jointheconversation.org Airport security email from Skeeter Skeeter Murphy to adam More options 2/24/05 (8 hours ago) Adam, Regarding stupid security checks at the airport (DSC-2005-02-21), check out Bruce Schneier's book, "Beyond Fear". He's a security guy and agrees that most of what gets implemented in the name of security is bogus. http://www.schneier.com/book-beyondfear.html > Over the last two years we've become obsessed with security, and put > in place a whole host of policies and procedures that will do... > exactly what? In his latest book, BEYOND FEAR, security expert Bruce > Schneier explains how security really works. The key is to think of > security not in absolutes, but in terms of sensible trade-offs, > whether on a personal or global scale. Schneier's practical approach > to problem-solving is a refreshing antidote to today's doomsday > pessimism and anxiety. With the technical know-how and common sense > that have made him one of the world's top security experts, Schneier > shows how we can move beyond fear to start thinking sensibly and > creatively about security. Hope that's interesting for you. Have a good day... Skeeter Seattle visit NDAs Jan Polet Jan Polet's Hit Test Hit Test 15 Nicholas Otto Duration: 00:31:31

item.itunes:title: Daily Source Code for Monday February 14th 2005
item.dc:creator: Adam Curry
item.description: Show details Podcast on February 14th 2005 From Guildford, Curry Cottage Direct download link Podcast feed Weblog Email MP3 Submissions and feedback No Stinkin' Transmitters - OpenPodcast.org #554 5th generation of RnR Adam's Podcasting Sweeper Rockmaninov Opener Go Home Productions Jacko Under Pressure riaa is watching us email Mjmaslar@aol.com to adam Show options Feb 10 (2 days ago) Adam, I thought you'd get a kick out of this email I'm the guy from Muze that's been harassing Bob Lefsetz to get into Podcasting. Lefsetz writes a very, very influential newsletter to all the top RIAA industry types. My CEO, Paul Zullo turned me onto him. As I've been evangizling RSS & Podcasting to him, he had the opportunity to go to his (Lefsetz) annual confab in Aspen this past December. When one of the heads of a major label got up to speak, he asked, "Who in here has heard of RSS & Podcasting?" My boss, and our SVP of Marketing were the only 2 to raise their hands out of a total of 130. Just thought you'd like to know that word is spreading.... Matthew Maslar ---------- Forwarded message ---------- From: Lefsetz@aol.com To: undisclosed-recipients:; Date: Wed, 9 Feb 2005 22:31:11 EST Subject: Dawn and Drew I was planning to go out hiking tonight but I might have to stay home. You see I'm hooked on DAWN AND DREW! There's this guy at Muze. He keeps bugging me. I've got to get into PODCASTING! I'm not sure I can get into ANYTHING fathered by Adam Curry. I can never forget that hair on MTV. But you don't have to download the software, bone up on tech to listen to podcasts. Hell, you can just listen to them as MP3s on your computer. I mean that's what I do whenever anybody e-mails me about these things. But now I'm hooked. I might have to download the software. To put all 70 shows on my iPod. Dawn and Drew ARE JUST THAT RIVETING! Did you ever know anybody in love? God, are you reading "Blink"? Freaks me right out. The part where they talk about whether a marriage is going to last. The key element is CONTEMPT! Oh, it's very hard to read the signals. You've got to be a pro. But once you're clued in, you know that slight roll of the eyeball, that slight brow lift, that evidences contempt. And the marriage is doomed. My marriage was doomed by contempt. My ex-wife was just TOO UNTOGETHER! I would get frustrated. Couldn't you PLEASE lock the door when you leave the house? I've got TENS OF THOUSANDS OF DOLLARS WORTH OF SHIT IN HERE! But, as many times as I mentioned it, she always continued to leave the door unlocked. Whew! I guess a marriage has to be based on mutual respect. And I'm not sure I've ever had that relationship. You know, one that fits like an old penny loafer. Where you're COMFORTABLE with each other. Oh, it doesn't mean you never disagree, it's just that you're IN IT TOGETHER! TWO people foraging in the forest instead of one. A BEST BUDDY WITH FRINGE BENEFITS! It appears Dawn and Drew are in love. Or maybe it's just that I'm infatuated with Dawn. Maybe she really wears the pants. Maybe Drew is kind of passive. But Dawn is a dream. First and foremost, she's VERBAL! I hate the silent babes. Hell, silences drive me NUTS! I want to be with someone who's got something to SAY! So I don't feel like an idiot when I comment on the minutiae of my life, when I spin my theories, make my observations. Dawn can keep up her end of a conversation. But she's not didactic. She's not overbearing. She's kind of like... You know, the kind of girlfriend you can't stop BUMPING INTO on the couch! They say stuff to bug you the tiniest little bit, to get under your skin just a little, because they KNOW YOU! THAT'S WHY THEY'RE DOING IT! You just want to slide your hip over and BUMP HERS! As evidence of INTIMACY! As evidence of CONNECTION! Dawn talks about the world at large. About her family. About her adventures. And sex. But not in a porn star way. In a NORMAL WAY! Sex is illegal in the United States. Don't they have a JUST SAY NO campaign? The government can't pass out condoms. Pornography must be stopped. But we're sex-centric. It's in our BIOLOGY! I mean she starts talking about a sideways vulva... How would you have sex with a woman like THAT! And then Drew kicks right in. About the MERMAID baby. The one with its legs fused. And Dawn plays dumb. Saying SHE'S NOT REALLY A MERMAID, IS SHE? Oh, you LOVE people like this. You just want to SQUEEZE HER!!! JUMP HER!!! She's so fucking ENDEARING! And then she starts talking about this wild dream she had. Where she orgasmed to a candy bar. And it wasn't even one she liked. And she starts quizzing Drew about wet dreams. And he's both uptight and DOESN'T KNOW SHIT! I mean for the first ten minutes or so, it was kind of boring. Well, not exactly boring. Kind of like sitting in a college dorm room with your buds. Interesting, familiar, but not RIVETING! But then Dawn is so open you can't HELP but listen. Because this is what you want. This openness in your OWN LIFE! Now I'll post articles below where you can catch up on this phenomenon. But I recommend you start where I did. Go to dawnanddrew.com. No, just listen to the podcast I did. Plug: http://mp3.dndshow.com/DNDS20050207.mp3 into your browser. Answer e-mail while you listen. Surf the Web. Do stuff in the background. SLOWLY, you'll get hooked. It's kind of like radio in the forties. But with a twenty first century twist. People are taking radio into their own hands and speaking from their hearts, UNFILTERED! A savvy radio station would add Dawn and Drew TOMORROW! And not change a fucking thing. Oh, by the way, you'll see pictures of Dawn and Drew in the articles below. Dawn doesn't look like a porn star. She's got purple hair and is thick. Completely changes your sense of beauty. Hell, I guarantee you I'd be better off with Dawn Miceli than Pamela Anderson and the Desperate Housewives. Because Dawn is real. And not afraid to be herself. Just another woman on the planet. http://www.usatoday.com/life/lifestyle/2005-02-08-podcasting_x.htm http://www.jsonline.com/onwisconsin/music/feb05/300150.asp fun with audio hijack Selling stuff comments Senseo email Brian Froeber to adam Show options 5:05pm (5 minutes ago) Adam, I just wanted to write you because I heard you mentioned your senseo coffee machine on your podcast recently. I got one recently through a website that links to a Yahoo group called Freecycle.org.... Basically its a link site to local Yahoo groups where people post usable items that they want to get rid of but don't want to mess with trying to sell it so they will post it up for grabs and if your looking for something, you can post a want ad and people will respond. bottom line is it has to be free. Its a great site and Im not sure if its worthy of mention on The Daily Source Code, but I think it might be to help boost membership worldwide as they have groups for all over the world. Back to the Senseo... The lady I got mine from had it for a month and didn't like the coffee it made... she said it was too "european". Well whatever!! So she offered it and I grabbed it... I haven't tried it yet but will soon. I was going to see if you were aware that there are 3rd party pod sites for flavored coffee, tea pods, and plastic adapters to make your own pod with self ground coffee.... I don't have links to them this moment but I was wondering if you have bought any pods from these sites, and if so, which sites do you like the best for purchasing pods?? I want to stay away from the 4 basic "flavors" that Senseo makes for the machine and explore alternative pods and pod accessories.... So what else do you use in your Senseo??? Also I love the daily source code and keep up the great work! Brian Froeber P.S. Do you remember a record label from the '80s named Enigma Records and are you familiar with any of the bands they had??? I know you played Mojo Nixon before. David DebateGod.com DebateGod Podcast Promo kevin c tofel kct's digital world Adam, please don't mention my podcast BBC The world launches podcast Podcast feed Site Cindy & Erwin are a couple Nimiq doesn't follow opml links in ts browser Renamarie and Canis Lupus Duration: 00:37:49

item.description: Show details Podcast on February 11th 2005 From Guildford, Curry Cottage Direct download link Podcast feed Weblog Email MP3 Submissions and feedback No Stinkin' Transmitters - OpenPodcast.org #554 5th generation of RnR Adam's Podcasting Sweeper Rockmaninov Opener .mac is hosed I fear PrinceJet Senseo email Joerg Steger to adam Show options 3:24pm (15 minutes ago) Hi Adam! You've done a nice job promoting the Philips Senseo coffee machine. I've actually bought myself one today and was completely blown away by the great taste of my first cup of Senseo coffee! Just one question, what kind of flavor do you prefer? I'm not quite sure which one to take. I took the regular red pads with me and I don't know if there are better ones. Greets from Germany, Devan & Kris Johnson Say Yum Say Yum - promo for Adam Curry WinAmp podcast solution email Frank Siedlaczek to adam Show options 4:22pm (2 hours ago) Adam, I thought your listeners might be interested in a freeware podcasting recording setup for Windows XP. It consists of 3 Winamp instances, a mixer (and optionally - the windows mixer dialogs for playback and recording. Note: To run 3 winamp instances at the same time, make sure to activate 'Allow multiple instances'. Then start them with the /NEW option on the command line (or parameter in the desktop link). The 3-way-mixer (it¹s called fcMixer) allows all three winamps to play simultaneously. This can be used to mix music with trailers, prerecorded material or sound effects as needed. It can do automated crossfading of the connected winamp instances you select. Even the speed of the automated blend can be configured. But of course, you can do the fading by hand, if you are a virtuos mouse user. In the first winamp I have loaded a music playlist, in the second I collected a few sound effects. The third winamp is configured to use its built-in Input plugin called CD/LineIn. This way, it¹s possible to do the voice recording with a microphone. fcMixer than mixes all that together at the current levels. How is the whole stuff recorded? I am using All2Wav (available from www.download.com). It can record everything that¹s being played on the soundcard. You can specify the quality of the recording and you are all set for a live podcast recording! All of the components are freeware! Isn¹t that nice ;-) WinAmp www.winamp.com (I recommend version 2.80full, it¹s fast and it works) fcMixer http://www.winamp.com/plugins/details.php?id=71153&download=yes&url=http%3A%2F%2Fdownload.nullsoft.com%2Fcustomize%2Fcomponent%2F2001%2F7%2F10%2FP%2FfcMixer.exe All2Wav http://www.download.com/3001-2168_4-10267687.html I¹ll attach a screenshot of my recording setup. Regards Frank Radio Glossary site Michael Ryan Duration: 00:38:57

item.description: Show details Podcast on February 10th 2005 From Guildford, Curry Cottage Direct download link Podcast feed Weblog Email MP3 Submissions and feedback No Stinkin' Transmitters - OpenPodcast.org #554 5th generation of RnR Adam's Podcasting Sweeper Rockmaninov Opener ASCAP License Jason's calculation New comment posted on CURRY.COM. Commenter's name: Jason Email address: markzero@gmail.com Commenting on: Daily Source Code for February 8th 2005 - I think the license says .0185 is the multiplier, which means 1.85%. It's still money, but not as scary. It's still subject to the minimum $288. MUCH SCARIER is the idea that this license says it's experimental. So, when they decide not to renew podcaster's license after the first period, they've acquired a lis t of names of people to watch and go after if they don't accede to later demands. Be careful before you go down that road... - Saying you think MJ was framed is one thing, but giving one reason you think that is because he's a "musical prophet" is pretty weak. So is saying you met the guy. (I'm sure a lot of people will say they've met the kids in the case, and the kids wouldn't lie, either.) If the evidence is weak or nonexistent, great, pound on that. But saying, essentially, 'he could never do that, because I like the guy' is just not a good reason. Plenty of "pillars of the community" have murdered, raped, etc., in the past, you know. item.dc:creator: Adam Curry
item.description: [00:01]Show details Podcast on February 6th 2005 From Guildford, Curry Cottage Direct download link Podcast feed Weblog Email MP3 Submissions and feedback No Stinkin' Transmitters - OpenPodcast.org #554 5th generation of RnR Adam's Podcasting Sweeper Rockmaninov Opener definitive cowbell Chambers Brothers - Cowbell of the day Time Has Come Today email Greg DelSesto Adam, Your listeners' cow bell submissions have been ... well, cute. But PLEASE, the seminal cow bell song, and the best cow bell song, is of course: "Time Has Come Today" by the Chambers Brothers, 1968, Columbia Records. The album version was "an 11-minute psychedelic soul epic." You, on the other hand, were 4 years old; your life barely longer than the length of this song. Please play the intro for your listeners so that we can lay the cow bell topic to rest; nothing else competes. Greg in Boston MJJ iriver embedding shownotes email From: Karleen, Dan Subject: mp3 caption editor for show notes Date: February 3, 2005 3:23:59 PM GMT+00:00 To: Adam Curry Love the DSC. Regarding the idea about embedding show notes, check out http://www.iriveramerica.com/support/cd/caption_editor.aspx. It looks like it lets you sync text with audio. Dan Karleen Morrisville, PA email Tom Schuring to adam Show options Feb 3 (9 hours ago) hey adam, the 'old' synchronised lyric standard (SYLT frame) in the ID3 (v2.3) embeds a 'file' into the ID3 tag so it is included into the mp3 you don't need to add an extra file so there is no synch problem the 'file' embedded contains the lyrics and a timecode. i have been searching for a good 1) editor to add this to any mp3 2) an itunes plugin that will show the lyrics when i play them 3) apple to include this stuff in the ipod. 1) and 2) can be done but i guess 3) will be pretty hard.. i am working on java program for 1). if it is any good i'll share.. (i'm using http://jid3.blinkenlights.org/ if anyone else wants to play along) for 2) i know there is a SYLT plugin for Winamp playes so i hope i can find one for itunes http://sites.rapidus.net/gpatrick/1.3.0/ReadMe.html ==================================== there is also another standard developed that will let you queue up and show images on a timecode (and heaps more from what i understand) http://www.id3.org/lyrics3200.html so that might be cool for the sight-seeing tours ==================================== cheers, email From: Olivier Anh Subject: MP3 player & lyrics Date: February 3, 2005 11:44:30 AM GMT+00:00 To: Adam Curry Reply-To: Olivier Anh Hi Adam, I'm just listening to your DSC of Feb 2nd. About the lyrics displayed in the some media players, this is a rather simple hack :) Beside the audio file (let's say bla.mp3), you just add a text file containing the lyrics, with the same filename (ie bla.txt). One sung phrase per line. That's all :) .lrc file format is another way for lyrics. Some karaoke and media players like Winamp (through a plugin, http://winamplyrics.hit.bg/info_eng.html) can read these files. lrc file is a plain text file like the above : one sung phrase per line. It just adds a time line, allowing to display the phrase at the right time, when the song is played :) Here's a link to the only site I can find right now... Sorry that's in french (As I'm french :) ) http://michbuze.club.fr/123/kar.htm#lrc (( Format LRC )) Here is how looks like such a file : [00:01]Celine Dion - My Heart Will Go On [00:20]Every night in my dreams [00:24]I see you, I feel you [00:29]That is how I know you go on. Below : compatible softwares iRiver seem to have its own format : SNC here a link in english : http://www.wu-wien.ac.at/usr/h00b/h0053049/sncpage/index.htm BTW : Yesss, you''re listened in France (in Bordeaux at least) \o/ Thanks for your show ! Keep going Olivier -- french listener Where are the chicks? email Hi Adam, I'm stuck at home with the flu today so I've been ego-surfing online to see where my podcast is listed and I found a neat link. Have you ever wondered where all the lady podcasters are? I guess Madge counts, but really, there are tons of us out there. Amy over at her blog Contentious has done us all a favor by compiling a list. That's one thing us girls do really well, make lists. So, here's hoping you get a minute to check out and plug some of the girlie podcasts! Kim C. (of Shakespeare Souffle and Homeschool Habitat) Here's the link; http://blog.contentious.com/archives/2004/12/22/women-in-podcasting-the-list 50 Pence I See Biddies Reality shows and anatomy for dummies email Cindy Casares to adam Show options Feb 4 (8 hours ago) Hi Adam, I don't know if anyone has replied to your comments about the autopsy show on Channel 4 or your reality show idea where celebs try to quit smoking, but there have been some shows to that effect televised in the States. On a somewhat obscure cable network called Trio, there were several episodes of televised autopsies that I saw last year. I couldn't really watch for long periods of time, but I kept sneaking peeks at it like some kind of accident on the highway. Unfortunately I can't find any references to it online, but I definitely watched it last year. It was on a lot and the doctor was German so I bet it was the same show you're watching over there. Also, another somewhat obscure cable network called PAX, which is usually a Christian network, has gotten in on the reality act with a show called Cold Turkey, where regular people try to quit smoking. And there was an ad campaign last year called Bob Quits that positioned itself as a reality show that people could watch online to see this guy Bob try to quit smoking. So, they were actually the first ones to do it in America that I know of. No celebs yet, but that can't be far behind since we already have celebrity weight loss shows on VH1. Cold Turkey http://www.pax.tv/shows/coldturk/ Bob Quits http://www.bobquits.com/skins/bobquits/home.aspx Trio Network http://www.trioplus.tv/plus/ email Todd Allaria to adam Hey Adam, Just wanted to mention that a Stop Smoking Reality show has already aired. It was pretty interesting. Each of the guests thought they were coming for a different reality until they were hit with the truth. Here is a link to the site. http://www.paxtv.com/shows/coldturk/ Love the show, Todd -- Todd P. Allaria todd@allaria.com www.allaria.com/ Jody Paulson - the fed (What they don't tell you) the fed David Dawson On The Wing 200501 Kent Ponds Soundseeing Tour typing cont. email Andrew Pulrang to adam Show options 5:18am (21 2 hours ago) Adam -- I took typing in high school, around the time you were a VJ on MTV. I never became really proficient ... I'd be the world's worst secretary ... but I did learn to touch-type, and I don't look at the keys. My typing teacher cured me of that in one day simply by taping a sheet of paper along the top of the keyboard, and draping it over my hands as I typed. That's it. Give it a try. Oh, and remember the "home row" ... asdf and jkl; Cheers! Andrew D. Pulrang AHP continued hugoschotman-hijacks#4005E0 Hugo's email From: Hugo Schotman Subject: Podcasting studio setup: about Audio Hijack Pro Date: February 3, 2005 9:54:47 AM GMT+00:00 To: qcarnicelli@rogueamoeba.com Cc: Adam Curry , dawnanddrewshow@gmail.com, Dave Slusher Hello Quentin, In response to your post about recording podcasts, here are some ideas. ( http://www.rogueamoeba.com/utm/posts/Linked/record-a-podcast ) The value of AHP for Podcasters can be increased by: 1. Keeping the application as it is. 2. Modifying the existing application in some key areas. 3. A complete overhaul of the functionality so it becomes a Podcaster's dream studio. Let me address these points in more detail. 1. Keeping the application as it is. Surprise ;) Actually, having tested the application quite a bit, I think it is already pretty good. What could make it better without changing the actual application is for us to know how to put it to best use. For me as somebody with a fair technical understanding if I would know more about the inner workings of the application I could easily optimize my configuration. For the less technically inclined, this would have to be translated into easy setup descriptions and 'Do's & Don'ts'. Concretely, what we should know right now (what I've been trying to figure out by trial and error) is: - Where does latency occur? - What buffers are there in the application and how big are they? - How can I get the least amount of latency from Mic input through some microhpone effects to my headphones? - What causes the increase in latency that sometimes occurs? (Reset by turning hijack on the microhpone off and on again.) - What affects the encoding and recording part and how can we make it most stable and least CPU/ Harddisk intensive? My current reference setup can be read here... http://log.hugoschotman.com/hugo/2005/02/low_latency_pod.html ...and heard here: http://log.hugoschotman.com/hugo/2005/02/low_latency_wit.html The audio files also contain a narrated tour through the setup. 2. Modifying the existing application in some key areas. Taking the questions from point 1. if these concerns can be made more visible in the user interface it would make the whole user experience better. For example: - Add buffer indicators to the 'source' and 'effects' setup screens. Preferably calculating the delay in miliseconds. - It would be nice if the application showed the cumulative latency in miliseconds for the signal that goes to the headphones. - Add CPU activity and I/O activity monitors with warnings for critical situations. - Add the possibility to configure the application's system scheduling priority. (See also: the 'nice' command in the shell/ terminal.) - Inside AHP, give sufficient priority to the signal that is being sent to the headphones. - Detect and correct changes in latency to the headphones. Note that some of the comments above are described with my configuration in mind. Please let me know if something is unclear. 3. A complete overhaul of the functionality so it becomes a Podcaster's dream studio. This would probably mean including the soundflower functionality in the application, include a mixer, include media players, etc. That would be a next step and would require input from several podcasters, including non-techies. Hopefully you can do something with these comments. Please let me know if I can be of more assistance. A diagram of my setup will follow within a few days. I've CC-d some people who are also working towards a better studio setup and who could maybe add some comments. Have fun, Hugo -- Hugo Schotman http://log.hugoschotman.com/ hugo.schotman@mac.com iChat/ AIM: hschot@mac.com Skype: hschot Tel. +41 76 430 1570 (mobile) - John Ong Duration: 01:16:36

item.description: Show details Podcast on February 3d 2005 From Guildford, Curry Cottage Direct download link Podcast feed Weblog Email MP3 Submissions and feedback No Stinkin' Transmitters - OpenPodcast.org #554 5th generation of RnR Adam's Podcasting Sweeper Rockmaninov Opener Thursday Trivia Day! Tapdancin' News OpenPodcast.org #856 typing blind squip From: squipper@nyc.rr.com Subject: Learning to type without looking Date: February 2, 2005 5:02:59 PM GMT+00:00 To: Adam Curry Adam, It will be easy for you to break the habit of looking at the keys while you type! Just get yourself a poster-size keyboard layout that you can hang on a wall in front of your laptop or desktop. Force yourself to look up at the poster and NOT at the keyboard. You'll get the hang of it in no time! http://www.speedskin.com/html/posters.asp Jeff Nemcher - Cooking on the Radio Sound seeing tours with iPod Photo Question for Adam about iPhoto satt bandwidth email From: Rob Frieden Subject: Satellite Capacity Measurement Date: February 2, 2005 6:27:06 PM GMT+00:00 To: Adam Curry Hello Adam: I very much enjoy The Daily Source Code and have an answer to your question about how satellite bandwidth is measured. The unit of capacity for satellites is the transponder, and these units are measured in MegaHertz, usually 36-72 MHz. Of course you can make a conversion from bandwidth to throughput which in a digital environment is measured in bits per second. I am a Telecoms Professor at Penn State University and teach this stuff; you might have an interest in a tech course syllabus on my web page at: http://www.personal.psu.edu/faculty/r/m/rmf5/Comm484spring05.htm Best wishes, Rob Frieden Pioneers Chair and Professor of Telecommunications Penn State University 102 Carnegie Building, University Park, PA 16802 office: (814) 863-7996; fax (814) 863-8161 home: (814) 867-2545 Web page: http://www.personal.psu.edu/faculty/r/m/rmf5/ Faculty profile: http://www.psu.edu/dept/comm/faculty/frieden.html adamcurryJaime Brad Sucks www.bradsucks.net Total Breakdown (demo) Trivia! hit test 4 80's tv theme quiz lost1 week trivia Lyrics trivia Rockmaninov Closer Duration: 00:41:02

item.description: 1.5 bold 1.5 1.5 20 italic Show details Podcast on February 2nd 2005 From Guildford, Curry Cottage Direct download link Podcast feed Weblog Email MP3 Submissions and feedback No Stinkin' Transmitters - OpenPodcast.org #554 5th generation of RnR Adam's Podcasting Sweeper Rockmaninov Opener Joan Jett & The Blackhearts Bad Reputation You Don't Own Me Steve Leeds Update Blue Man Group update email From: Sebastian Wiesinger Subject: Blue Man Group Date: January 31, 2005 10:22:33 PM GMT+00:00 To: Adam Curry Hi Adam, greetings from Germany. :) First let me tell you that I love your podcast, keep up the great work. On your podcast 2005-01-31 you played a track from Blue Man Group with Vocals from Venus Hum. That track is actually from the Complex Rock Tour Live: http://www.amazon.com/exec/obidos/tg/detail/-/B0000DBJ9P This is an awesome DVD and the music on it is just great. This is *not* the normal show program in Las Vegas but a special "Rock Tour" which Blue Man Group did. If you can get this DVD watch it, its great. I saw the german edition of the Blue Man Group theater program, that also kicks ass, but it's more show than music in it. Auf Wiedersehen from Germany, Sebastian -- GPG Key-ID: 0x76B79F20 (0x1B6034F476B79F20) Wehret den Anfaengen: http://odem.org/informationsfreiheit/ Thunder rolled. ... It rolled a six. --Terry Pratchett, Guards! Guards! Dave Lee Apocalpse Radio Country msn search email From: Simon Speight Subject: MSN Search Date: February 2, 2005 11:32:44 AM GMT+00:00 To: Adam Curry Hi Adam, Saw your blog posting about the fact that MSN Search redirects you to the UK version since you're now a fellow Brit :) I tried it today and got the same results you did. Got half an answer for you - try visiting this address: http://search.msn.com/?noredir=1 This will let you search the whole "inkernet" (nice phrase ;-) and find the same search results that Dave did. Plus, it seems to set a cookie so that the next time you visit http://search.msn.com it won't redirect you to the UK version. Its a solution but I agree that its a bit lame. I prefer the way Google does it - search the whole damn thing unless *I* say so. Cheers, Simon Speight dsc-lyric-shownotes-#3F487D Windows security Christiaan Stoudt HomeNetworkHelp.Info 2005-02-01-AdamCurryComments sillycambridgeplug Badwell Ash - Take AHP I'm a blind typer It's very limiting hit test 3 celebrity stop smoking reality show Clare Fader & The Vaudevillains Site email From: Mary K. Elkins Subject: girl & cello = sexy, you say? Date: February 1, 2005 8:35:17 PM GMT+00:00 To: Adam Curry Hi Adam, My girlfriend LeeAnn Westover turned me on to your podcast. My friend and former co-worker Adam Howell spoke over the cube to me back in November about podcasts, rss feeds, and you specifically. At that point I was working 80hr+ weeks trying to figure out how to quit my full time job, so i could freelance webdesign full time (www.missmaryk.com). SO needless to say, I nodded and continued making my Honda Banner Ads and scheming on different creative ways to quit. (One idea, make the poll on the front of the website say "How cool is it that i just quit?") Sadly, his & LW's talk of this "podcasting" was absorbed only minmally. I live in Winston-Salem, NC on the Southside where artists and musicians can own whole houses. I live here with my boyfriend Daniel VonSeggen (vonseggen.com) and my 2 alien ragdoll cats Omar and Aladdin. There are some photos of them on my photo weblog (www.lame-oh.com). Here they are with Biddy Amanda Monaco on a recent visit: (http://206.130.97.180/mk/lo/2005/01/omar-is-part-squirrel.html) I play cello (wheeet-whooooo) in a "New Generation Cabaret" band called Clare Fader & The Vaudevillains. If you like the idea of music which includes girl-on-cello-action, you'll love us. Anyway, fastforward a few months. I have finally had the chance to begin to embrace podcasting. I love it! I find myself getting very jacked up when thinking about the exciting possibilities ahead. My brain hurts when i think about all of the freedoms and ways to get our music heard that are there via podcasting that are only usually spoken about in misty, remember-when, elvis-sun studios-stories. About a month ago, my close friend Jeffrey Dean Foster (www.jeffreydeanfoster.com) -- another fine NC musician -- emailed me about reading the new Dylan book, Chronicles. This is what he said in his email, that has recently come to my mind this week listening to your podcasts. * "I got the Dylan Chronicles book from Kitty. It is so enjoyable to read and yet really makes these times in music seem pretty lightweight and inconsequential. I had visions of a NYC somewhat like that when I was young and when we finally did get there it was pretty exciting. Dark and cold most of the time but warm in the clubs. full of possibilities. I've got to invent some new possibilities. they seem to be a dying species sometimes." *So I just wanted to introduce myself, my band and say a big thanks for helping invent some new possibilities for us musicians making music off the radar. Big time. Love, Mary K. Elkins Clare Fader & The Vaudevillains Seventh and Trade Betty Crocker's Bail Rockmaninov Closer Duration: 00:47:51

item.description: 1.5 bold 1.5 1.5 20 italic Show details Podcast on January 31st 2005 From Guildford, Curry Cottage Direct download link Podcast feed Weblog Email MP3 Submissions and feedback 5th generation of RnR No Stinkin' Transmitters - OpenPodcast.org #554 Adam's Podcasting Sweeper Rockmaninov Opener Bette Midler, Goldie Hawn, & D You Don't Own Me The PC Audio inspector plugin email Adam, Here's a workaround tip for better audio clip level control. As you know from your many years in the business, -12 dB is the Broadcast Standard for output level. With this knowledge in hand, you should re-record your clips to the proper -12 dB and watch your production value increase. Download this FREE AU plugin application: http://www.elementalaudio.com/products/inspector/index.html 1. Once installed, use your Effects settings in Audio Hijack Pro to insert "Inspector". 2. Use the "Inspector" gain control to adjust gain input/output to -12 dB on the meters. (avg.) 3. Re-record the audio clips. You could also adjust dB on the fly but you would have to be quick on the "Inspector" gain control. Don't blow out my ears and remember this, the iPod's volume control is not that accessible so a little extra time in pre-production goes a long way in audience appreciation. -Greg Walker Anatomy for beginners Grant Baciocco & Dougg Price Duration: 00:43:30

We have had one show up for 5 days and are already one of the highest rated student radio shows in the university. Martha thanks to Rich Graham Mojo Nixon & Skid Roper Stuffin' Martha's Muffin Shownotes integration idea email Gabe Kangas to me Show options 4:16am (5 hours ago) Hey Adam, Wanted to send you a quick audio comment/show promo to tell you about a couple new things i'm doing over at my show "The r33tcast". Due to your discussion of show notes in the past, I setup a system that I feel works really well. As each person subscribes to the show they enter their email address. This email address gets saved and they in return get a custom RSS feed to subscribe to. Then, as each show is downloaded they receive, in thier email, the show notes for that show after it's been downloaded. If they chose to unsubscribe, or skip certain shows, they receive no show notes. I really feel a system like this is what would add a lot to the integration of text and audio. Also, for novelty sake, I thought you might like the other "first" that's going on over at the r33tcast, virtual co-hosts that speak via chat throughout the whole thing. It's very cool. I'm still working out the bugs, but it's definitely a first. One real voice, many "not so real". Hope all is well, stay r33t! Gabe Kangas Weds trivia answers (Jan Polet) hit-test-answers 60s trivia email David Dawson to me Show options Jan 27 (14 hours ago) Adam attached is a .mp3 file with a few 60s tunes for you to identify. item.description: Show details Podcast on January 18th 2005 From Guildford, Curry Cottage Direct download link Torrent link Podcast feed Weblog Email No Stinkin' Transmitters - OpenPodcast.org #554 Adam's Podcasting Sweeper Rockmaninov Opener Jamie Foxx, not Farr! Easynet phone calls BT Easynet Farrah Fawcett lawsuit Stuart Hunter Trivia From: Stuart Hunter Subject: Name That Tune - Answers Date: January 18, 2005 5:52:54 AM GMT+00:00 To: Adam Curry Reply-To: Stuart Hunter Hey, Adam - that was fun, thanks very much for playing my bit - I do like it when podcasts get interactive. I think there are a lot of folks like me out there who don't really have the inclination to commit to undertaking a regular podcast but sometimes come up with stuff that is suitable for inclusion in an established podcast such as yours. I had great fun doing the bit and I hope the listeners got into it as well. Anyway here are the answers 1: Morrissey - Every Day is Like Sunday 2: Wet Wet Wet - Love Is All Around 3: Visage - Fade to Gray 4: Mental As Anything - Live It Up 5: John Farnham - The Voice 6: Icehouse - Hey Little Girl 7: The Connels - 74, 75 8: Black - Wonderful Life Regards. Stuart Ken Gantz and his Arbtron diary Adam, Hopefully I will go down in podcasting history as the first person to document a podcasted show in my Arbitron radio diary. I had really hoped that I would be able to list the DSC in the diary but couldn't get around the fact that one of the pieces of data they require for each entry is whether the show is on AM or FM. I was afraid that including the DSC might invalidate the diary. I wound up listing my other favorite podcast done by Leo Laporte on KFI 640 AM in Los Angeles. I also made a note in the comments section of the diary explaining how podcasting makes it possible for me to listen to a radio station in Los Angeles while living in Louisville, KY. I finished by including a quote that I think is suitable a bumper sticker (do they have bumper stickers in Europe?). "Podcasting expands radio's reach." Note in the attached screenshot how Arbitron doesn't even know the word "Podcast". They will after this week! Cheers, Ken Gantz SoundSeeing continued email about Murrow Dear Adam, Hello from snowy Rhode Island. I was listening to your podcast today and was rather intrigued to hear your Edward R. Murrow clip posted from another listener. I dont know if you know about his history at CBS or the structure of radio at that time, (I assume that as a professional in radio you probably already do) but before Murrow came to CBS, radio was very much scripted and edited down with little or no live brodcasts at all. Its all very interesting to see how he began to pioneer the "soundseeing" that you yourself are now taking an interest in. Bob Edwards, the long time NPR voice on Morning Edition actually wrote a book on Murrow entitled "Edward R. Murrow and the Birth of Broadcast Journalism" that was an excellent read and also quoted the very broadcast that you podcasted today. Anyhow, just thought I'd drop you a line on that one. Oh, and it was Jamie Fox, not Jamie Farr; but you probably got about 50 other corrections on that one. Keep up the great work, you have pretty much become my afternoon commute. Best Regards, Ryan Napolitano ryan@pcraftdental.com ps. In regards to your search for GPS interface, you may want to research the garmin ique 500 (not sure on that model #), which is a gps/palm device that has some quirky little options on it. Also, have you heard of the cell phone project in NYC that tags numbers on locations, and when you call them, you are given a little audio snippet? I was hearing a buzz on this sometime back but ran out of interest until you popped that little idea into my head. The GPS sync shouldn't be too out of reach though....my handheld GPS allows me to connect text notes to locations. soundseeingtour.com Adam Bloom's suggestions From: Adam Bloom Subject: GPS service you mentioned Date: January 18, 2005 6:23:09 AM GMT+00:00 To: Adam Curry Cc: Ron Bloom adam, On DSC-2005-01-17, you mentioned an idea linking GPS to podcasting. there's something called "geofencing" services../I think it's what you are looking for. example scenario: you walk with your GPS/Cell/PDA across this "virtual fence" and your mobile unit notifies a server...then the server can email you a notification with a link or whatever. some more info on solutions in this area...esri actually has posted some sample code for how you access their network to do something like this. http://www.accutracking.com/ http://support.esri.com/index.cfm?fa=downloads.samplesUtilities.viewSample&PID=20&MetaID=890 http://www.ulocate.com/technology.html http://tuxedo.esri.com/geofence/ http://www.snaptrack.com/ http://tuxedo.esri.com/geofence/ http://www.hstcglobal.com/pdf/ptld.pdf ab paul podcast paul promo podcastpaul.promo Podsafe Music From: Adam Christianson Subject: New Canadian Artist receiving good feedback after playing on my Podcast Date: January 18, 2005 8:11:24 AM GMT+00:00 To: Adam Curry Reply-To: Adam Christianson Adam, In trying to promote new artists in Podcasting I recently played music from one of the listeners to my Podcast, The MacCast (http://www.maccast.com), and I am getting great resonse to his stuff. A couple of listeners are buying his CDs. Anyway if you want to check out Jim Bryson, http://www.jimbryson.org and listen to his stuff. It has got a country feel and I think it's good. Easynet phone calls BT Easynet Farrah Fawcett lawsuit Stuart Hunter Trivia - From: Stuart Hunter - Subject: Name That Tune - Answers - Date: January 18, 2005 5:52:54 AM GMT+00:00 - To: Adam Curry - Reply-To: Stuart Hunter - Hey, Adam - that was fun, thanks very much for playing my bit - I do - like it when podcasts get interactive. - I think there are a lot of folks like me out there who don't really - have the inclination to commit to undertaking a regular podcast but - sometimes come up with stuff that is suitable for inclusion in an - established podcast such as yours. - I had great fun doing the bit and I hope the listeners got into it as well. - Anyway here are the answers - 1: Morrissey - Every Day is Like Sunday - 2: Wet Wet Wet - Love Is All Around - 3: Visage - Fade to Gray - 4: Mental As Anything - Live It Up - 5: John Farnham - The Voice - 6: Icehouse - Hey Little Girl - 7: The Connels - 74, 75 - 8: Black - Wonderful Life - Regards. - Stuart Ken Gantz and his Arbtron diary - Adam, - Hopefully I will go down in podcasting history as the first person to document a podcasted show in my Arbitron radio diary. I had really hoped that I would be able to list the DSC in the diary but couldn't get around the fact that one of the pieces of data they require for each entry is whether the show is on AM or FM. I was afraid that including the DSC might invalidate the diary. - I wound up listing my other favorite podcast done by Leo Laporte on KFI 640 AM in Los Angeles. I also made a note in the comments section of the diary explaining how podcasting makes it possible for me to listen to a radio station in Los Angeles while living in Louisville, KY. I finished by including a quote that I think is suitable a bumper sticker (do they have bumper stickers in Europe?). "Podcasting expands radio's reach." - Note in the attached screenshot how Arbitron doesn't even know the word "Podcast". They will after this week! - Cheers, - Ken Gantz SoundSeeing continued - email about Murrow - Dear Adam, - ?? Hello from snowy Rhode Island.? I was listening to your podcast today and was rather intrigued to hear your Edward R. Murrow clip posted from another listener.? I dont know if you know about his history at CBS or the structure of radio at that time, (I assume that as a professional in radio you probably already do) but before Murrow came to CBS, radio was very much scripted and edited down with little or no live brodcasts at all.? Its all very interesting to see how he began to pioneer the "soundseeing" that you yourself are now taking an interest in.? Bob Edwards, the long? time NPR voice on Morning Edition actually wrote a book on Murrow entitled "Edward R. Murrow and the Birth of Broadcast Journalism" that was an excellent read and also quoted the very broadcast that you podcasted today.? Anyhow, just thought I'd drop you a line on that one.? Oh, and it was Jamie Fox, not Jamie Farr; but you probably got about 50 other corrections on that one.? Keep up the great work, you have pretty much become my afternoon commute. - Best Regards, - Ryan Napolitano - ryan@pcraftdental.com - ps.? It has been a few years since I flew EZ Jet on the segment from Edinburgh to Schiphol, via Gatwick. - The experience was as you described: polite, efficient, and orderly. However, the plane was smaller: one aisle with two seats on each side. - The entertainment go roaring once the plane left the gate. A group made up of family and friends were traveling to a football match and celebrating a birthday, at the same time. Although the policy is for drink sales only on the plane, the flight attendant allowed for a special exception - after much begging from the already tipsy husband. He brought a bottle of champaign onto the plane and asked if it could be put on ice and served. - In the middle of the flight, the chanpaign was served "secretly" - at the request of the flight attendant - and with fanfare, by the enthusiastic husband - and friends. After two rounds of champaign "down the hatch" and glasses clinking, the football cheers and pep songs began. And supporters of opposing teams sang out their favorite tunes. It was an enjoyable flight. And the crew did not mind at all. A different flying experience. - You are right. It was in experience that might occur on a bus, rather than in the air. - Thank you for raising my curoisity in podcasting. I heard your interview over WNYC or National Public Radio, not too long ago. - Date: December 31, 2004 12:36:18 AM GMT+00:00 - To: Adam Curry - Hey Adam - - Do you know if any podcasters will be doing anything at SXSW in Austin Tx this year? - The Biddies will be playing a showcase and hanging out that week, and we'd love to check anything podcast-related out, or maybe help promote it.... - Lee Ann - www.Biddies4Ever.com for all things Biddy - Online Press Resource: www.biddies4ever.com/pk.html - Including high-res photos, MP3s, bios, video & more! - "Manhattan's hippest Girl Group" - The Washington Post - "Angelic vocal harmonies, wordy humor, jazz chops and pop moxie" - Time Out New York - "Quirkiness, cuteness and classic elegance" - The Pittsburgh City Paper Chutes are for sissies - email - From: AJ Orr - Subject: parachutes are for sissies - Date: December 30, 2004 6:44:05 PM GMT+00:00 - To: Adam Curry - Dear Adam, - Your comments on your December 28th Daily Source Code concerning the parachutes was right on. - I am a crew chief on a UH-60 (Black Hawk) MEDEVAC helicopter. I am currently winding down my second tour in Iraq, my third to the Middle East, and I have never even considered a parachute as an option. (Even if a parachute was possible in our bird it would be foolish.) - Granted there is a huge difference in fixed wing and rotary wing aircraft when it comes to emergency procedures, namely, a fixed-wing aircraft has glide characteristics by it's very design without engine power whereas a rotary-wing bird has the glide characteristics of a rock. Autorotation is our parachute. - I've had passengers ask me about "our parachutes." I always laugh at this because it's totally amusing. We fly so low and, 95% of the time at speeds of 160 knots or more, that if something was to go wrong, even if there was a parachute that would deploy with any acceptable usefulness 50 feet off the ground it would be completely entangled in a potentially mangled rotor system anyhow. In an emergency the only thing we have time to do is lock our harness reels and pray the pilots up front are doing the right thing. - I am also nearly finished with my FAA private pilot certification and the thought of a parachute on my bird seems fairly ridiculous. I can just see someone having an engine malfunction, freaking out, ignoring the emergency procedures section of their checklist, and popping this chute at 2,000 feet over a populated area. Not only will they be seriously injured, or killed, but so will dozens, maybe even hundreds, of innocents below both from the impact and the ensuing fire. - You also mentioned that the seats were rated to absorb 30Gs of impact. That's all well and good but a human body can not handle an impact of more than around 11 Gs. So unless those seats are magically distributing 20+ Gs of force, the passengers/crew of said bird are going to be seriously injured, perhaps even more so than if they had attempted an emergency landing. - I am by no means a mathematical genius and don't know with what kind of force a parachuting aircraft will impact but on the whole this parachute idea sounds like a very bad one. - For $16,000 a pilot could get a ton more training, both in the aircraft and out, from qualified instructors who would instill in them a sense of confidence and level-headedness that could prevent them from ever getting into a situation requiring such a silly device. Take for example the US Air Force crew that landed the EP-3 in China several years ago. Because their bird was so messed up they did aerobatic maneuvers that it was NEVER designed to do. But because of their superb training, attention to detail and keeping their wits about them they were able to safely land a totally unflyable aircraft. - That money could be better spent elsewhere. - Respectfully, - Sergeant AJ Orr - Balad, Iraq Joan Nicolai - pocast comments - Comment on Senseo item on DCS 2004-12-29 adamemail Rockmaninov Closer

#title "DSC-2004-12-30" Show details - Podcast on December 30th 2004 - From Curry Cottage, Guildford UK - Direct download link - Torrent link - Podcast feed - Weblog - Email Radio scan sweeper Adam's Podcasting Sweeper Rockmaninov Opener Welcome BBC readers Boston Phoenix article Drum Battle - email - From: Joel Hawksley - Subject: music for your podcast - Date: December 29, 2004 9:15:01 PM GMT+00:00 - To: Adam Curry - Adam, - here's a "famous" drum cadence from the movie /Drumline/ (by fox, a must - see movie btw) - liscence: probably mpaa, but who cares - title: The Classic Drum Battle - -joel - Drumline - Drumline - The Classic Drum Battle Howard Stern on Letterman More sample rate stuff - FLEB comment - New comment posted on CURRY.COM. - Commenter's?name:? - FLEB - Email?address:? - arcticdoom@pixelsaredead.com - Web?site:? - http://www.voterudy.org - IP?address:? - 63.90.115.89 - Domain?name:? - 63.90.115.89 - Commenting?on:? - Daily Source Code for December 29th 2004 - Regarding the MP3 warble problem: I don't know how much of this you know or don't know (I'm sure a lot of it's old news to you, but someone else here might be able to use this info), so I'll just run down everything I know. I'm not a pro, but this is what I know from what I picked up. -- You're getting all the warble because you changed the SAMPLE rate of the audio, but not the BITrate of the compression. That means you have more raw, uncompressed audio going in, hence it needs to be compressed more aggressively. The SAMPLE rate measures the rate of the individual voltage readings that make up a waveform. For example, CD quality audio is 44100Hz, or 44100 samples per second. The practical sound application of sample rate is that the highest frequency you can represent digitally is the sample rate divided by 2. (This highest frequency would be a simple square wave: one sample for the high point, one sample for the low point.) Although the human ear cuts off at around 11-12kHz, some people can tell a difference in tone and quality between a 22050 (highest freq: 11025Hz) and a 44100 (highest freq: 22050Hz) sound file. The practical data application of sample rate is that, basically, samples are data. A uncompressed file with a higher sample rate has more data than one with a lower sample rate. This comes into play in your situation when you try to compress them down. The BITRATE is a bit different. Fundamentally, the bit rate has nothing to do with the "sound" that's being produced. It's simply a measure of "How much data does one second of sound take up?". Compression attempts to shrink the size (number of bits) per second of audio, making the uncompressed audio, (at about 705.6kbps for CD-quality audio) into a file at 64kbps or 128kbps MP3s that you're used to. When you tell the MP3 compressor you want a 64kbps file, you're telling it, "Compress this raw audio, whatever it is, enough that one second will take up 64000 bits." Basically, you're setting the size of the "box", and the MP3 compressor stuffs your audio down small enough to fit. When you had the downsampling to 21000Hz sample rate, there were fewer samples per second, and therefore less raw audio data that the compressor had to fit in that 64kb "box". When you turned that off, however, it was trying to cram almost twice as much raw data (the 44100Hz-rate original file) into the same-size 64kbps "box". The only way to achieve that was to apply more squeeze to it. Since MP3 is lossy compression, more compression means more loss, and you get the signature MP3 warble. My advice would be to set the the process up to make 22050Hz files, which is a more common sample rate, and should (hopefully) work on people's portables. You really don't need that sound quality up in the 11050-22050Hz frequencies for something as talk-based as what you're doing. Alternatively, you could look into making VBR (Variable BitRate) MP3 files, which analyze each frame of audio and pick the best bitrate for good-sounding compression. This podcast sounded horrible with compression artifacts evident all over the place. I'm sure you know that with the same bitrate at a higher sampling rate you are now having to encode far more information than what LAME can accomplish by automatically applying it's defaults to the source material it's given. LAME has become the best over the years because it's defaults have been tweaked to death to provide the best sound for any material it's been given and the preset handed to it. And when you start getting into lower bitrates such as 64k and lower, you have to start cutting either channels or sampling rate in order to keep it sounding decent. So I would say either the 24 setting or find a way to force 22.050 or the warbles are sure to drive a bunch of us mad. Addiction to alcohol & pain killers....... - CNN Violet Blue Podcast - violet blue - open source sex - Direct download link Madge Weinstein - Yeast Radio - Yeast Radio:Naked Podcasting Delay! - paul's email - From: Paul Eastman - Subject: Del-l-lay - Date: December 27, 2004 1:41:34 AM GMT+00:00 - To: Adam Curry - Hi Adam, - Hope you had a great festive period. - Firstly, I'd like to tell you how cool it was to hear our tune 'come see - about me' on your last Daily Source Code before xmas. Our first PodCast! - Many thanx. - I've been thinking about the problem you have with the slight delay in your - headphones while recording your PodCast. I can't be sure, but this sounds - like a problem faced by all musicians when recording a live performance - directly to a computer, called 'Latency'. This is generated by the vast - amount of processing the computer has to do to the audio data before it - reaches your headphones. Looking at the diagram of your set-up, it seems - there's a fare few applications the audio is passing through before it - finally reaches the output stage. - This can be incredibly off-putting for, let's say, a singer who wants to - listen to their own voice during a recording session. - There are a few ways to get round this problem; the one I use is to have a - mixer at the input stage and take a split off to the singers headphones, the - same as taking the headphones out of your audio interface I guess. The mix - to the computer from this input mixer is sent via an auxiliary output which - enables you to bring the computer output back into the mixer, without the - vocals, so you can listen to the audio clips you drop in during the show. - You might have to put a bit of effects at the input stage just so you have - an idea how your voice is sounding, but doesn't end up in the final mix! - So you listen to you voice real-time through dedicated effects (with no - Latency) while everything else comes from computer. Clear as mud?! - Mmn, I think that kinda makes sense. If indeed it is the Latency problem. - Anyways, thanks again for the play, and hope some of this info is of use. - Respect to the Bastian of Boing! - Paul@AudioDesigners.co.uk dv 122704 64 - Wisonsin news Airplane chutes - From: Mike Corley - Subject: Linkage!
